Stage 4 Bipin Chandra India Since Independence Ch 6-38 — 113 additions (Kamaraj, Syndicate, Congress split 1969, Emergency-era MISA/ADM Jabalpur/Turkman Gate, Janata, Mandal 1979, Rajiv accords, Bofors, IPKF, Dravidian + Left Front + Kashmir politics, Bipin economy)
Stage 5 Laxmikanth temporal polity — 47 additions (17 amendments 1950-90, 8 landmark cases, 6 constitutional institutions, 3 emergency invocations, 6 structural provisions)
Stage 6 Ramesh Singh economy — 20 additions (IPR 1948/1956, Mahalanobis Plan, LIC/SBI 1955-56, IDBI/ICICI/IFCI/NABARD/SIDBI DFI stack, wage-employment schemes, BOP buildup)
Stage 7 Nitin Singhania — 12 additions (Husain, Raza, Ghatak, Sen, Benegal, NCPA, ICCR, SAI, 1982 Asiad, 1983 Cricket WC, Doordarshan, AIR)

Stage 12 source-based gap audit — 28 additions verified against Laxmikanth/Ramesh Singh/Bipin Chandra grep counts (5 Presidents, CBI/CVC/Santhanam/ARC-I/Kaka Kalelkar/NDC/ISC/Zonal Councils/CAT/Law Commission, IPR 1977+1980, Essential Commodities Act, Operation Barga, ULFA, Aryabhata/Rohini/INSAT/Kalam/DRDO/CSIR/Ramanna, Rajiv-Jayewardene Accord)

build_summary.boundaries: Start: 15 Aug 1947 (Independence). End: 1991 — 1990 Mandal implementation + 1991 BOP crisis are era-boundary. Liberalisation (LPG July 1991) begins era 11.
build_summary.temporal_polity_streams: 3 dedicated lanes (s11 Amendments, s12 Cases, s13 Institutions) — largest use yet of the temporal-polity architecture (era 9 had 1 lane).

nodes.label: Nation-Building & Integration (1947-52)
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Five years of consolidating a torn nation. Independence + Partition (15 Aug 1947), Kashmir accession (Oct 1947), Gandhi's assassination (30 Jan 1948), RSS ban. Hyderabad Police Action (Sept 1948), Junagadh plebiscite. Objectives Resolution → Constitution adopted 26 Nov 1949, commenced 26 Jan 1950. First general elections 1951-52 under Sukumar Sen. 'Steel frame' IAS takes shape. Patel's integration machine (V.P. Menon). Refugee crisis.

nodes.label: Nehru Era — Domestic (1951-62)
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Nehruvian project: mixed economy, democratic socialism, secular state. First 3 FYPs + Mahalanobis model (Second Plan 1956-61 heavy industry). Avadi 1955 (socialistic pattern), Nagpur 1959 (cooperative farming). IPR 1948/1956. Community Development Programme 1952. Hindu Code Bills 1955-56. Dams (Bhakra, Hirakud, DVC) + steel plants (Bhilai/Rourkela/Durgapur). Mundhra scandal 1957. SRC 1956. First President's Rule (Kerala 1959). Jana Sangh 1951, Swatantra 1959.

nodes.label: Nehru Era — Foreign Policy (1947-62)
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Non-aligned vision articulated. Panchsheel (1954) with Zhou Enlai. Bandung Conference 1955 (Afro-Asian solidarity). Suez Crisis 1956 response. Dalai Lama asylum 1959. Forward Policy 1961. 1962 India-China War — McMahon Line dispute, disastrous defeat. Krishna Menon resigned. Goa liberation 1961. Nehru's death May 1964 as coda.

nodes.label: Shastri Interregnum (1964-66)
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Brief but consequential. Kamaraj Plan 1963 prepared succession. Shastri PM June 1964. 1965 Indo-Pak War (stalemate, water-tight defence). Jai Jawan Jai Kisan. Green Revolution seeds sown — FCI + APC 1965, C. Subramaniam + Swaminathan + Borlaug. Tashkent Agreement Jan 1966. Shastri's sudden death 11 Jan 1966. Nanda acting PM twice.

nodes.label: Indira I (Congress Split → 1971)
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Indira chosen as 'gungi gudiya' (1966) — turned out otherwise. Rupee devaluation June 1966 (politically disastrous). 1967 elections broke Congress System. 1969 Congress split (R vs O) over V.V. Giri presidential election. Bank Nationalisation 1969, Privy Purses abolished 1971 (26th Amendment). Garibi Hatao slogan → 1971 landslide (352 seats). Bangladesh War 1971 → Bangladesh Liberation. Indo-Soviet Treaty Aug 1971. 24th-26th Amendments (1971) reasserting Parliament supremacy. Kesavananda Bharati (April 1973) established basic structure doctrine.

nodes.label: Emergency (1975-77)
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Constitutional breakdown. Allahabad HC 12 June 1975 voided Indira's election. Emergency declared 25 June 1975 — 21 months of suspended FRs, mass detention under MISA (110,000+), press censorship, ADM Jabalpur (1976). 42nd Amendment 'Mini-Constitution' (Dec 1976) — Socialist+Secular+Integrity to Preamble, Fundamental Duties, DPSPs over FRs. Sanjay Gandhi's 5-point — forced sterilisation (8.3M), Turkman Gate demolitions. Ended with Jan 1977 election call and Indira's defeat March 1977.

nodes.label: Janata + 44th Amendment (1977-80)
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: First non-Congress govt. Morarji Desai PM (81). Shah Commission (Emergency excesses). 44th Amendment 1978 reversed 42nd — restored judicial review, written cabinet advice for Emergency, 'armed rebellion' (not 'internal disturbance'), right to property out of FRs. Mandal Commission appointed Dec 1978 (report submitted 1980, shelved). Janata split July 1979 over dual-membership. Charan Singh 28 July 1979 - Jan 1980 (shortest PM, never faced Parliament). 1980 elections returned Indira.

nodes.label: Indira II + Punjab + Assassination (1980-84)
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Indira's return. Second bank nationalisation April 1980 (6 more banks). Sanjay's death June 1980 — Rajiv reluctantly enters politics. Punjab crisis intensifies — Bhindranwale + Akali Dal + Anandpur Sahib (1973) agitation. Operation Blue Star 1-8 June 1984 at Golden Temple. Indira assassinated 31 Oct 1984 by Sikh bodyguards. 1984 anti-Sikh riots Nov — 2,733+ killed Delhi. Bhopal Gas Tragedy 3 Dec 1984. Asiad 1982 + Cricket WC 1983.

nodes.label: Rajiv Years (1984-89)
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Youngest PM (40). Computer revolution, telecom push (C-DOT, Sam Pitroda). Three Accords 1985-86: Assam (14 Aug 1985, cutoff 25 March 1971), Punjab (Rajiv-Longowal 24 July 1985 — Longowal assassinated Aug), Mizo (30 June 1986 — Laldenga CM). 52nd Amendment 1985 Anti-Defection Law. Shah Bano reversal → Muslim Women Act 1986. Shilanyas at Ayodhya Nov 1989. IPKF in Sri Lanka 1987-90. Bofors scandal broke April 1987. V.P. Singh resigned, broke away. 1989 elections — Congress lost.

nodes.label: V.P. Singh + Mandal (1989-90)
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: National Front minority govt with BJP + Left outside support. 7 Aug 1990 — implemented Mandal Commission 27% OBC reservation. Upper-caste backlash — Rajiv Goswami self-immolation Sept 1990 + 159 more. Advani's Rath Yatra (Sept-Oct 1990) toward Ayodhya — arrested in Bihar by Lalu Yadav 23 Oct. BJP withdrew support, VP Singh govt fell 7 Nov 1990. Chandra Shekhar interim govt. BOP crisis building — forex down to 15 days imports by June 1991. Rajiv assassinated 21 May 1991. 1991 elections + LPG reforms = era-11 opening.

nodes.label: Constitutional Amendments (1951-91)
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: 65 amendments 1951-1990. Four themes: (1) State reorganisation — 7th Act 1956, 9th Berubari, 12-14th UTs, 22nd Meghalaya, 27th Arunachal-Mizoram, 35-36th Sikkim. (2) SC/ST/OBC reservation extensions — 8th, 23rd, 45th, 51st, 62nd. (3) Land reform / 9th Schedule — 1st, 4th, 17th, 29th, 34th, 40th, 47th, 66th. (4) Emergency + judicial — 24th-26th (Indira), 38th-42nd (authoritarian), 43rd-44th (Janata restoration). 52nd Anti-Defection (1985), 58th Hindi Constitution (1987), 61st voting age 18 (1989).

nodes.label: Landmark SC Cases (1950-1992)
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Pillars of constitutional jurisprudence. A.K. Gopalan 1950 (narrow Art 21). Champakam Dorairajan 1951 → 1st Amendment. Romesh Thappar 1950 (free speech). Shankari Prasad 1951 → Sajjan Singh 1965 (FR amendment power upheld) → Golaknath 1967 (reversed). Berubari 1960 (territory cession + Preamble role). Kesavananda Bharati 24 April 1973 — basic structure doctrine (7-6). Indira-Raj Narain 1975 applied it. ADM Jabalpur 1976 (Emergency habeas corpus — SC's darkest). Maneka Gandhi 1978 (procedural + substantive due process). Minerva Mills 1980. Waman Rao 1981 (9th Schedule line). Shah Bano 1985. Indra Sawhney 1992 (Mandal upheld, 50% cap).

nodes.label: Constitutional Institutions (1950-1990)
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Bodies that operationalised the Constitution: Election Commission of India (25 Jan 1950), CAG (1950), UPSC (1950), Finance Commission (first 1951, Neogy), Planning Commission (15 March 1950). All India Services — IAS/IPS continuation, IFoS added 1966. Swaran Singh Committee 1976 (42nd amendment blueprint). Sarkaria Commission 1983 (Centre-State relations). National Commission for Women 1990. Key laws: Citizenship Act 1955, Preventive Detention Act 1950, Official Languages Act 1963/1967, NSA 1980. 9th Schedule (1951) and 10th Schedule (1985) added by amendment.

nodes.label: Planning & Economy
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: From Nehruvian self-reliance to pre-LPG. Industrial Policy Resolutions 1948/1956. Seven FYPs + Plan Holiday (1966-69) + Rolling Plan. Mahalanobis model (heavy industry). PSU ecosystem — SBI 1955, LIC 1956, IFCI 1948, ICICI 1955, IDBI 1964, NABARD 1982, SIDBI 1990. Bank Nationalisation 1969 + 1980 (20 banks, 91% deposits). Licence-Permit-Quota Raj. MRTP 1969 (Dutt/Hazari findings). FERA 1973. 1966 Devaluation. 'Hindu rate of growth' 3.5%. Dams-steel plants (Bhakra/Hirakud/DVC/Bhilai-Rourkela-Durgapur). BOP crisis build-up 1985-91 → 1991 reforms.

nodes.label: Land Reforms & Agrarian (Green/White Rev)
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Three phases of land reform: (1) Zamindari Abolition 1950s (UP 1950, Bihar 1950, WB 1953) — first success. (2) Ceiling Acts — weak except WB/Kerala. (3) Consolidation + Bhoodan (Vinoba's 4.4M acres from 1951, Pochampalli origin, Gramdan extension). Green Revolution ecosystem from 1966: HYV (Borlaug + Swaminathan + Subramaniam), FCI 1965, APC/CACP 1965, MSP from 1966-67. White Revolution / Operation Flood (Kurien, NDDB 1965, AMUL) three phases 1970-96 made India world's largest milk producer. Maharashtra EGS 1972 → IRDP 1978, NREP 1980, RLEGP 1983, JRY 1989.

nodes.label: Linguistic Reorganisation & Language
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Potti Sriramulu's 58-day fast-unto-death (died 15 Dec 1952) → Andhra state Oct 1953. Fazal Ali Commission (SRC) 1953 → States Reorganisation Act 1956 (14 states + 6 UTs). Nagaland 1963, Haryana+Punjab split 1966, 7 sister states NE reorganised 1971-72. Anti-Hindi agitations in Tamil Nadu 1965 → Official Languages Act 1967 guaranteed English continuation. 21st Amendment 1967 added Sindhi to 8th Schedule, 71st Amendment 1992 added Konkani+Manipuri+Nepali. 58th Amendment 1987 gave Hindi Constitution legal sanctity. Three Language Formula (Kothari Commission 1966).

nodes.label: Science & Technology
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Three-stage nuclear programme (Homi Bhabha): TIFR 1945, AEC 1948, AEET/BARC 1954 — Apsara reactor 1956 (first in Asia), CIRUS, Dhruva. Pokhran-I 'Smiling Buddha' 18 May 1974 (Raja Ramanna). Space programme (Vikram Sarabhai): INCOSPAR 1962, PRL Ahmedabad 1947, ISRO 15 Aug 1969, Aryabhata 1975 (Soviet launch), Rohini SLV-3 1980 (first indigenous launch), INSAT-1A 1982. Green Revolution technology (HYV seeds). CSIR network expansion.

nodes.label: State Politics (Dravidian, Left Front, Kashmir)
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Dravidian politics: Periyar's DK 1944 → Annadurai's DMK 1949. DMK swept TN 1967 after anti-Hindi agitation — ended Congress rule permanently. MGR's AIADMK split 1972. TN alternates DMK-AIADMK ever since. Andhra: NTR's TDP 1982 swept 1983 on Telugu pride — first non-Congress AP govt. WB: Left Front won 1977 (CPI(M) 231/294), Jyoti Basu CM 23 years. World's longest democratically-elected communist govt until 2011. J&K: Sheikh Abdullah dismissed 1953, jailed to 1968, Indira-Abdullah Accord 1975. Farooq succeeded 1982. Dismissed 1984 by Jagmohan. Naxalbari uprising May 1967.

nodes.label: Regional Insurgencies & Accords
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Punjab Crisis: Akali Dal founded 1920, Anandpur Sahib Resolution 1973, Bhindranwale → Operation Blue Star June 1984, 1984 riots, Rajiv-Longowal Accord 24 July 1985 (Longowal assassinated). NE insurgencies: Naga (Phizo's NNC 1955, Nagaland 1963, Shillong Accord 1975), Assam movement 1979-85 → Assam Accord 14 Aug 1985 (cutoff 25 March 1971) → AGP 1985. Mizo National Front — 20-year insurgency → Mizo Accord 30 June 1986 (Laldenga CM, Mizoram statehood 1987). Most successful accord. Kashmir insurgency ignited 1989 (era-11).

nodes.label: Social Movements (Environment, Women, Dalit)
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Environmental: Chipko 1973 (Reni village, Bhatt + Bahuguna + Gaura Devi) → Forest Conservation Act 1980. Silent Valley campaign (Kerala 1970s-80s) → scrapped 1981 + national park 1984. Narmada Bachao Andolan from 1985 (Medha Patkar) against Sardar Sarovar. Women's: Towards Equality Report 1974 (Phulrenu Guha) → feminist awakening. Mathura Rape Case 1972/1979 → Criminal Law (Second Amendment) 1983. Dalit: Dalit Panthers 1972 (Maharashtra), Namantar Andolan, Kanshi Ram's BAMCEF 1971 → DS4 1981 → BSP 1984. SC/ST Prevention of Atrocities Act 1989. JP Movement 1974 + Naxalite Movement continuation.

nodes.label: Communalism & Ram Janmabhoomi
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Communal trajectory. Gandhi's assassination 30 Jan 1948 (Godse, ex-RSS) → RSS ban Feb 1948-Jul 1949. Major post-independence riots: 1969 Ahmedabad (500-2000 killed), Bhiwandi 1970, Moradabad 1980. Shah Bano reversal (1986 Muslim Women Act) perceived as minority appeasement. VHP-led Ram Janmabhoomi movement from early 1980s. Shilanyas Nov 1989 at Babri site. Advani's Rath Yatra Sept-Oct 1990 (arrested by Lalu). Babri Masjid demolition 6 Dec 1992 (era-11 boundary). BJP's rise from 2 seats (1984) to 85 (1989) to 121 (1991).

nodes.label: Art, Literature, Cinema, Media
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Modern Indian art rebirth. Progressive Artists' Group Bombay 1947 (Souza + Ara + Raza + Husain + Bakre + Gade) — break from Bengal School, modernist idiom. Three akademis 1952-54: Sangeet Natak, Sahitya, Lalit Kala + ICCR 1950. Parallel cinema wave: Satyajit Ray's Pather Panchali 1955 (Apu Trilogy), Ritwik Ghatak, Mrinal Sen's Bhuvan Shome 1969 (kicked off FFC funding), Shyam Benegal from 1974 (Ankur, Nishant, Manthan — crowdfunded). Broadcasting: Akashvani 1957, Doordarshan 1959 (colour 1982 Asiad, national channel 1984). 1982 Asian Games + 1983 Cricket WC = mass spectacle era.

nodes.label: Parallel — Cold War & NAM
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Bipolar world. Truman Doctrine 1947, Marshall Plan 1948, NATO 1949 / Warsaw Pact 1955. Korean War 1950-53. Khrushchev's secret speech 1956. Hungarian + Suez crises 1956. Sputnik 1957. U2 1960. Cuban Missile Crisis Oct 1962. Prague Spring 1968. SALT I 1972. Helsinki Accords 1975. Soviet Afghan invasion 1979. Gorbachev 1985, Glasnost+Perestroika. Berlin Wall fell 9 Nov 1989. USSR dissolved Dec 1991. NAM: Bandung 1955, Belgrade 1961 (Nehru-Tito-Nasser), continued through 17 summits. G-77 (1964), NIEO 1974. India-USSR strategic tilt via 1971 Treaty. UN bodies (UNGA, UNSC, UNSG). IMF/WB/GATT → WTO 1995.

nodes.label: Parallel — China (CCP → Deng)
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Mao's China arc. CCP revolution victory 1 Oct 1949 (PRC). Korean War involvement 1950-53. Hundred Flowers + Anti-Rightist 1957. Great Leap Forward 1958-62 (30-45M deaths, famine). Sino-Soviet split 1960. 1962 India-China War. Cultural Revolution 1966-76 (Red Guards, Gang of Four). Nixon visit Feb 1972 (US-China opening). Mao's death Sept 1976. Deng Xiaoping's return 1978 — Four Modernisations, SEZ Shenzhen 1980. Tiananmen Square June 1989. By 1991 China was quietly re-integrating via reform-and-opening while Soviet bloc collapsed.

nodes.label: Parallel — Decolonisation & Third World
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Wave of independences. Vietnam: Dien Bien Phu May 1954 (French out), Geneva 1954 split, US escalation 1964-73, Fall of Saigon 30 April 1975. Indonesia: Sukarno until Suharto's 1965 coup. Africa: Ghana 1957 (Nkrumah), Congo crisis 1960-65, Algeria 1962, decolonisation of 17 in 1960. Arab-Israeli: 1948, Six-Day 1967, Yom Kippur 1973. Iran Revolution 1979 (Khomeini). Latin America: Cuba 1959 (Castro), Allende Chile 1973 (Pinochet coup), dirty wars. Eastern Europe shake: Solidarity Poland 1980 (Walesa), Velvet Revolution Czechoslovakia 1989. Apartheid South Africa: Sharpeville 1960, Soweto 1976, Mandela released 1990, dismantled 1991-94.

nodes.label: Linguistic States
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Reorganisation of Indian states on the basis of language, primarily after 1956. Initially feared to cause disintegration, but actually made the country more united and administration easier. Some states created on basis of culture, ethnicity, or geography (Nagaland, Jharkhand).

nodes.label: Language Policy of India
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: No national language; Hindi is official language but mother tongue of only 40% Indians. 22 Scheduled Languages recognised. States have own official languages. Government exams can be taken in any scheduled language. Anti-Hindi agitation in Tamil Nadu (1965) led to continued use of English.

nodes.label: Civil Rights Movement (USA)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Movement from 1954-1968 aimed at abolishing legal racial discrimination against African-Americans. Led by Martin Luther King Jr., practiced non-violent civil disobedience. Succeeded in gaining equal legal rights. Tommie Smith and John Carlos raised Black Power fists at 1968 Olympics.

nodes.label: Black Power Movement
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: More militant anti-racist movement (1966-1975) advocating even violence if necessary to end racism in the US. Emerged alongside the Civil Rights Movement when progress was seen as too slow.

nodes.label: Northern Ireland Conflict
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Conflict between Nationalists (mostly Catholics wanting unification with Ireland) and Unionists (mostly Protestants wanting to remain in UK). Example of overlapping social differences (religion, class, nationality) leading to violent civil conflict.

nodes.label: Yugoslavia Disintegration
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Political leaders in Yugoslavia mobilised populations based on religious and ethnic identity, creating mutual hostility. Demands for separate nation-states led to disintegration of the country and a civil war. Shows how politics of social division can destroy national unity.

nodes.label: Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Founded in 1980 from former Bharatiya Jana Sangh. Ideology: cultural nationalism, Hindutva. Came to power at centre in 1998 as NDA leader. Became single largest party in India's multi-party system. Support base spread across North and West India.

nodes.label: Anti-Defection Law
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: 52nd Amendment (1985) introduced Tenth Schedule to prevent elected members from switching parties after elections. If a member defects, he/she loses seat. Aimed at reducing political instability and horse-trading. Has reduced but not eliminated defections.

nodes.label: Dr B.R. Ambedkar
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constitution. Played a decisive role in shaping the document. Advocated for parliamentary system, fundamental rights for marginalized. Called the 'Father of Indian Constitution'.

nodes.label: Adoption of Constitution
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Constitution adopted on November 26, 1949 (now celebrated as Constitution Day). Came into effect on January 26, 1950 (Republic Day), chosen to commemorate the Purna Swaraj declaration of 1930.

nodes.label: 42nd Amendment (1976)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Called 'Mini-Constitution' due to sweeping changes. Added 'Socialist', 'Secular', 'Integrity' to Preamble. Added Fundamental Duties. Curtailed judicial review. Many provisions reversed by 43rd and 44th Amendments.

nodes.label: Election Commission of India
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Independent constitutional body under Article 324. Supervises, directs and controls elections. Currently has CEC + 2 ECs. CEC can only be removed by impeachment (same as SC judge). Prepares electoral rolls, monitors model code of conduct.

nodes.label: Supreme Court of India
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Apex court of the Indian judicial system established under Part V, Chapter IV of the Constitution. Has original, appellate, advisory, and writ jurisdictions. Its decisions are binding on all courts in India. Can review its own judgments under Article 137. All authorities must act in aid of the Supreme Court under Article 144.

nodes.label: High Courts
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Each state or group of states has a High Court. High Courts can issue writs under Article 226 (wider scope than SC as they cover any other purpose beyond fundamental rights). Exercise superintendence over all subordinate courts. Hear appeals from district courts.

nodes.label: Hussainara Khatoon vs. Bihar (1979)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: One of the earliest PILs. Filed on behalf of under-trial prisoners in Bihar who had spent more time in jail than the maximum punishment for their alleged offences. Established right to speedy trial as a fundamental right under Article 21.

nodes.label: Kesavananda Bharati Case (1973)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Landmark 13-judge bench case that established the Basic Structure Doctrine. Ruled that Parliament can amend any part of Constitution but cannot destroy its basic structure. Right to property was held not part of basic structure. Court reserved to itself the right to decide what constitutes basic structure. Most important case in Indian constitutional law.

nodes.label: District and Subordinate Courts
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Lowest level in the judicial hierarchy. District courts deal with cases arising in the district, consider appeals from subordinate courts, and decide serious criminal offences. Subordinate courts handle civil and criminal cases at the lowest level. Function under superintendence and control of the High Court.

nodes.label: Bandhua Mukti Morcha vs. Union of India (1984)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Important PIL case decided by Justice Bhagwati. Addressed the issue of bonded labour. Court held that problems of the poor need a different kind of judicial approach and strict adversarial procedure would prevent them from enforcing fundamental rights. Expanded locus standi for public interest cases.

nodes.label: Sunil Batra vs. Delhi Administration (1980)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Pioneer PIL case. A Tihar jail inmate sent a scribbled letter to Justice Krishna Iyer about physical torture of prisoners. The judge got it converted into a petition. Established that even a letter can be treated as a writ petition if it concerns violation of fundamental rights.

nodes.label: Sarkaria Commission (1983)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Appointed by central government in 1983 to examine issues relating to centre-state relations. Submitted report in 1988. Key recommendation: appointments of Governors should be strictly non-partisan. Examined the misuse of Article 356 and recommended restraint in its use. Major reference point for centre-state relation reforms.

nodes.label: States Reorganisation Commission (1954)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Set up in 1954 to examine the question of reorganisation of states. Recommended creation of linguistic states at least for major linguistic groups. Led to the States Reorganisation Act, 1956. Marked the beginning of the process of creating states on linguistic basis.

nodes.label: Armed Forces Special Powers Act (AFSPA)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Made on the basis of Articles 33 and 34 which authorize Parliament to protect persons in service of union or state for actions during martial law. Has created tensions between people and armed forces in some regions. A manifestation of Union powers that can override normal federal arrangements in areas of conflict.

nodes.label: P.K. Thungon Committee (1989)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Recommended constitutional recognition for local government bodies in 1989. Advocated periodic elections to local bodies and enlistment of appropriate functions along with funds. Its recommendations formed the basis for the 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendment bills introduced in 1989.

nodes.label: Community Development Programme (1952)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Launched in 1952 to promote people participation in local development across a range of activities. Led to the recommendation of a three-tier Panchayati Raj system for rural areas. First systematic attempt at involving local communities in development planning in independent India.

nodes.label: 43rd and 44th Amendments (1977-78)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Passed after Janata Party came to power in 1977. Cancelled most controversial changes made by the 38th, 39th and 42nd amendments. Restored constitutional balance. 44th Amendment specifically: restored Lok Sabha term to 5 years, removed right to property from fundamental rights (made it legal right under Art 300A), strengthened safeguards against misuse of emergency provisions.

nodes.label: 52nd Amendment -- Anti-Defection (1985)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Added the Tenth Schedule to the Constitution dealing with disqualification of members on grounds of defection. A member who voluntarily gives up membership of the party or votes against party whip is disqualified. Decision rests with the Speaker/Chairman. Later modified by 91st Amendment (2003). Example of amendment through political consensus.

nodes.label: Minerva Mills Case (1980)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Supreme Court reaffirmed the basic structure doctrine from Kesavananda Bharati. Struck down provisions of the 42nd Amendment that attempted to override judicial review. Held that the balance between fundamental rights and directive principles is itself part of the basic structure. Established that limited amending power is a basic feature of the Constitution.

nodes.label: Amendment on Binding Nature of Council of Ministers Advice
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Article 74(1) was amended to clarify that the advice of the Council of Ministers will be binding on the President (President shall act in accordance with the advice). In reality, this was already the practice in parliamentary government. The amendment was only by way of explanation, making explicit what was implicit in the original Constitution.

nodes.label: 38th and 39th Amendments (1975)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Controversial amendments passed during the Emergency period. The 38th Amendment made the declaration of Emergency non-justiciable. The 39th Amendment placed the election of the President, Vice President, Prime Minister and Speaker beyond judicial scrutiny. Both were later largely reversed by the 43rd and 44th Amendments after the Emergency ended.

nodes.label: Universal Declaration of Human Rights
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Adopted by UN General Assembly in 1948. 30 articles covering civil, political, economic, social, and cultural rights. Not legally binding but morally authoritative. Inspired national constitutions and international covenants.

nodes.label: Cuban Missile Crisis
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: In 1962, the USSR placed nuclear missiles in Cuba, putting the US mainland under threat from close range. President Kennedy ordered a naval blockade. The crisis was the closest the Cold War came to nuclear war. Soviet ships turned back, averting catastrophe.

nodes.label: North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Western military alliance formed in April 1949 with 12 member states. An armed attack on any member in Europe or North America was regarded as an attack on all. Led by the US. Continues to exist post-Cold War.

nodes.label: Warsaw Pact
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Eastern military alliance led by the Soviet Union, created in 1955 to counter NATO forces in Europe. Included most East European communist states. Dissolved after the Cold War ended.

nodes.label: Southeast Asian Treaty Organisation (SEATO)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: US-led alliance in Southeast Asia, formed in 1954 as part of Cold War containment strategy. Aimed to prevent the spread of communism. Less effective than NATO, dissolved in 1977.

nodes.label: Central Treaty Organisation (CENTO)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Originally the Baghdad Pact (1955), a US-backed alliance in West Asia. Included UK, Turkey, Iran, Iraq, and Pakistan. Dissolved in 1979 after the Iranian Revolution.

nodes.label: Non-Aligned Movement (NAM)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Movement of newly decolonised countries choosing not to join either Cold War bloc. First summit in Belgrade 1961 with 25 members. Founded by Tito, Nehru, Nasser, Sukarno, and Nkrumah. Not isolationism or neutrality but active involvement in world affairs. Had 116 members by 2006.

nodes.label: Josip Broz Tito
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: President of Yugoslavia (1945-80). One of five founders of NAM. Communist leader who maintained independence from the Soviet Union. Key meeting with Nehru and Nasser in 1956 led to NAM.

nodes.label: Gamal Abdel Nasser
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Ruler of Egypt (1952-70). One of five founders of NAM. Championed Arab nationalism, socialism, and anti-imperialism. Nationalised the Suez Canal in 1956.

nodes.label: Kwame Nkrumah
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: First Prime Minister of Ghana (1952-66). One of five founders of NAM. Advocated socialism and African unity. Opposed neo-colonialism. Removed in a military coup.

nodes.label: UNCTAD
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: UN Conference on Trade and Development. Published 1972 report proposing reforms to make global trade beneficial for poorer countries. Institutional basis for NIEO demands.

nodes.label: Limited Test Ban Treaty (LTBT)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Signed in 1963 by US, UK, and USSR. Banned nuclear weapon tests in the atmosphere, outer space, and under water. One of the first major arms control agreements of the Cold War.

nodes.label: Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Signed 1968, in force 1970. Only five states that tested before 1967 may keep nuclear weapons. Extended indefinitely in 1995. India has not signed, considering it discriminatory.

nodes.label: Anti-Ballistic Missile (ABM) Treaty
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Part of SALT-I, signed 1972. Limited deployment of ABM systems, preventing their use as defensive shield to launch nuclear attacks. Maintained strategic stability.

nodes.label: Korean War
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: War 1950-53 between North Korea (backed by USSR and China) and South Korea (backed by US-led UN forces). Ended with division along 38th Parallel. Nehru played key mediating role.

nodes.label: Mikhail Gorbachev
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Last leader of the Soviet Union (1985-91). Introduced perestroika (restructuring) and glasnost (openness). Stopped the arms race with the US, withdrew troops from Afghanistan. His reforms inadvertently accelerated the disintegration of the USSR.

nodes.label: Perestroika and Glasnost
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Reform policies introduced by Gorbachev. Perestroika meant economic restructuring to modernise the Soviet economy. Glasnost meant political openness allowing freedom of expression. Together they loosened the system but set in motion forces that led to the USSR's collapse.

nodes.label: Fall of the Berlin Wall
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: The Berlin Wall, built in 1961 to separate East and West Berlin, was toppled by the people on 9 November 1989. Symbolised the end of the Cold War and the beginning of the collapse of the communist bloc in Eastern Europe.

nodes.label: Baltic States Independence
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania were the first Soviet republics to declare independence. Lithuania declared independence in March 1990. All three became UN members in September 1991 and later joined NATO in 2004 and the EU.

nodes.label: Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Established in 1967 by Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore, and Thailand (Bangkok Declaration). Later joined by Brunei, Vietnam, Laos, Myanmar, and Cambodia (10 members). Follows the ASEAN Way: informal, non-confrontationist, cooperative. Established ASEAN Regional Forum (ARF) in 1994.

nodes.label: China's Special Economic Zones (SEZs)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Zones where trade barriers were eliminated and foreign investors could set up enterprises. State played central role in setting up market economy. Led to phenomenal rise in foreign trade and FDI. China has 6 SEZs compared to India's 200+ approved SEZs.

nodes.label: Four Modernisations
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Proposed by Premier Zhou Enlai in 1973: modernisation of agriculture, industry, science and technology, and military. Laid the groundwork for Deng Xiaoping's subsequent economic reforms.

nodes.label: India-China Relations
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Border conflict in 1962 over Arunachal Pradesh and Aksai Chin had long-term implications. Relations improved after Rajiv Gandhi's 1988 visit. Bilateral trade grew from $338 million (1992) to $18 billion (2006). Both view themselves as rising powers. Boundary talks continue.

nodes.label: Japan as Economic Power
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Second largest economy in the world. Only Asian member of G-8. Second largest contributor to UN budget (nearly 20%). Security alliance with US since 1951. Article 9 of constitution renounces war. Despite low military spending (1% of GDP), fourth largest military expenditure globally.

nodes.label: US-China Relations (1972)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: China ended political and economic isolation by establishing relations with the US in 1972 when President Nixon visited China. This was a major shift in Cold War dynamics and preceded China's economic reforms.

nodes.label: Indus Waters Treaty
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Signed in 1960 between India and Pakistan with World Bank mediation. Governs sharing of rivers of the Indus basin. Has survived all military conflicts between the two countries. Minor differences on interpretation remain.

nodes.label: South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Regional cooperation initiative begun in 1985, headquartered in Kathmandu. Has not had much success due to persisting political differences, especially India-Pakistan tensions. Members signed SAFTA agreement for free trade zone.

nodes.label: India-Bangladesh Relations
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Differences over Ganga and Brahmaputra water sharing, illegal immigration, and Bangladesh's refusal to allow Indian troop transit to northeast. Farakka Treaty signed in 1996. Bangladesh part of India's Look East policy. Cooperation on disaster management improved.

nodes.label: India-Sri Lanka Relations
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Tensions over Tamil ethnic conflict. India sent IPKF in 1987 (withdrew 1989). Adopted policy of disengagement after IPKF failure. Free trade agreement signed. India's post-tsunami reconstruction aid improved ties.

nodes.label: Shimla Agreement
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Signed in 1972 between India and Pakistan after the 1971 war. Established that all issues between the two countries would be resolved bilaterally through peaceful means. Established the Line of Control in Kashmir.

nodes.label: Indian Peace Keeping Force (IPKF)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Indian troops sent to Sri Lanka in 1987 under an Indo-Sri Lanka accord to stabilise Tamil-Sinhala relations. Got into conflict with LTTE. Sri Lankans saw it as interference. Withdrew in 1989-90 without achieving objectives.

nodes.label: India's Intervention in Maldives
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: In November 1988, Tamil mercenaries from Sri Lanka attacked the Maldives. Indian air force and navy responded quickly to Maldives' request, stopping the invasion. India has contributed to the island's economic development.

nodes.label: Bangladesh Liberation War
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: In 1971, East Pakistan's demand for autonomy under Sheikh Mujib was crushed by Pakistani military. India supported independence movement financially and militarily. War in December 1971 ended with Pakistani surrender and creation of Bangladesh.

nodes.label: International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Established in 1957 to implement US President Eisenhower's Atoms for Peace proposal. Promotes peaceful use of nuclear energy and prevents military use. Teams regularly inspect nuclear facilities worldwide.

nodes.label: Biological Weapons Convention (BWC)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Signed in 1972. Banned the production and possession of biological weapons. Over 155 states acceded. Included all great powers. One of the key disarmament treaties alongside CWC.

nodes.label: Montreal Protocol
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: 1987 path-breaking agreement to protect the ozone layer by phasing out ozone-depleting substances like CFCs. Discovery of ozone hole over Antarctica in mid-1980s provided urgency. Considered one of the most successful environmental agreements.

nodes.label: Integration of Hyderabad
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: The Nizam of Hyderabad wanted independent status. After a peoples movement in the Telangana region and the Nizam refusal to accede, Indian army conducted Operation Polo in September 1948 to integrate the state.

nodes.label: Integration of Junagadh
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Junagadh was a small state in Gujarat whose Muslim ruler acceded to Pakistan despite having an overwhelmingly Hindu population. India conducted a plebiscite in which people voted to join India.

nodes.label: Integration of Manipur
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Manipur Maharaja Bodhchandra Singh signed the Instrument of Accession under pressure in 1949. The state had a democratically elected legislature which was not consulted, generating resentment among the people.

nodes.label: States Reorganisation Act (1956)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Following the States Reorganisation Commission (SRC) report of 1955, India reorganised its internal boundaries along linguistic lines in 1956. Preceded by formation of Andhra Pradesh in 1953 after Potti Sriramulu death. Created the modern map of Indian states.

nodes.label: Assassination of Mahatma Gandhi
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Mahatma Gandhi was assassinated on 30 January 1948 by Nathuram Godse, a Hindu extremist opposed to Gandhi pursuit of Hindu-Muslim unity. Gandhi death had a dramatic effect -- communal violence subsided, RSS was briefly banned, and communal politics lost appeal.

nodes.label: RSS Ban (1948)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: After Gandhi assassination, the Government cracked down on organisations spreading communal hatred. The RSS was banned for some time. Part of the broader effort to contain communal politics after Partition violence.

nodes.label: First General Election (1952)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: India's first general election held October 1951 to February 1952 was the biggest gamble in democratic history. 17 crore eligible voters (only 15% literate) elected 489 Lok Sabha MPs and 3200+ MLAs. Election Commission under Sukumar Sen conducted it. Over half the eligible voters turned out, proving democracy could work in a poor nation.

nodes.label: Socialist Party
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Originated from Congress Socialist Party (CSP) formed in 1934. Forced to separate in 1948 when Congress banned dual membership. Leaders included Jayaprakash Narayan, Rammanohar Lohia, Acharya Narendra Dev, Asoka Mehta. Advocated democratic socialism but faced a dilemma when Congress declared socialist pattern as its goal in 1955.

nodes.label: Communist Party of India (CPI)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Emerged in 1920s inspired by Bolshevik revolution. Won 16 seats in 1952, becoming largest opposition party. In 1957, CPI-led government in Kerala became the world's first democratically elected Communist government. Split in 1964 into CPI and CPI(M) following the Sino-Soviet rift.

nodes.label: Communist Government in Kerala (1957)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: E.M.S. Namboodiripad led CPI to victory in Kerala in 1957 -- the world's first democratically elected Communist government. Won 60 of 126 seats. Congress launched a 'liberation struggle' against it. In 1959, central government dismissed it under Article 356 -- widely cited as first misuse of emergency powers.

nodes.label: Bharatiya Jana Sangh
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Founded in 1951 by Shyama Prasad Mukherjee. Drew ideological inspiration from RSS. Emphasised one country, one culture, one nation and called for a uniform civil code. Initially limited to Hindi-speaking states and urban areas. Later merged into Janata Party in 1977 and its members formed BJP in 1980.

nodes.label: Swatantra Party
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Founded in 1959 by C. Rajagopalachari (Rajaji). First explicitly right-wing party, advocating free enterprise, opposing state intervention, planning and nationalisation. Drew support from former princes, landlords and industrialists.

nodes.label: Shyama Prasad Mukherjee
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Founder of Bharatiya Jana Sangh in 1951. Member of Nehru's first cabinet, resigned over the Nehru-Liaquat Pact. Opposed Article 370 granting special status to J&K. Died in 1953 while in detention in Kashmir.

nodes.label: CPI Split (1964)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: The Communist Party of India split in 1964 following the Sino-Soviet ideological rift and the India-China war of 1962. The pro-USSR faction remained as CPI. The pro-China faction formed CPI(M). Many CPI(M) leaders were arrested as pro-China.

nodes.label: E.M.S. Namboodiripad
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Leader of the Communist Party in Kerala who became Chief Minister in 1957, heading the world's first democratically elected Communist government. Initiated radical land reforms. His government was dismissed under Article 356 in 1959.

nodes.label: Sukumar Sen
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: First Chief Election Commissioner of India appointed in January 1950. Organised the mammoth first general election of 1952 with 17 crore voters. Trained over 3 lakh officers and devised the ballot-box-per-candidate system for largely illiterate voters.

nodes.label: C. Rajagopalachari (Rajaji)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Last Governor-General of India, senior Congress leader, and founder of the Swatantra Party in 1959. Opposed Congress socialist policies, especially state controls and the License Raj. Advocated free enterprise as the path to prosperity.

nodes.label: Avadi Resolution (1955)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: At its session in Avadi near Madras, Congress passed a resolution declaring socialist pattern of society as its goal. Reflected in the Second Five Year Plan. Made it difficult for the Socialist Party to differentiate itself from Congress.

nodes.label: Public Sector Development
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: State controlled key heavy industries -- steel plants, oil refineries, defence production, railways, electricity. Created commanding heights of the economy. Critics said it bred inefficiency, corruption through license-permit raj, and created a privileged middle class.

nodes.label: Import Substitution Strategy
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: India's development strategy emphasised producing domestically what was being imported. Substantial tariffs imposed on imports to protect domestic industries. Limited India's economic interaction with the outside world but helped domestic industries grow.

nodes.label: K.N. Raj
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Young economist involved in drafting the First Five Year Plan. Argued that India should hasten slowly for the first two decades as fast development might endanger democracy.

nodes.label: Chaudhary Charan Singh
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Congress leader who later broke away to form Bharatiya Lok Dal. Forcefully articulated the case for agriculture-centred planning. Argued planning created urban-industrial prosperity at the expense of farmers. Later became PM briefly in 1979.

nodes.label: J.C. Kumarappa
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Gandhian economist who proposed an alternative blueprint emphasising rural industrialisation. Author of Economy of Permanence. Member of the Planning Commission but his views represented the minority position.

nodes.label: Panchsheel (Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Five principles enunciated jointly by PM Nehru and Chinese Premier Zhou Enlai on 29 April 1954: mutual respect for territorial integrity, mutual non-aggression, mutual non-interference, equality and mutual benefit, and peaceful coexistence. Ironically preceded the India-China border conflict.

nodes.label: India-China War (1962)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: China launched a massive invasion in October 1962 on both Aksai-chin (Ladakh) and NEFA (Arunachal Pradesh). India suffered a humiliating defeat. Led to V.K. Krishna Menon's resignation as Defence Minister, a no-confidence motion against Nehru, and the CPI split. India approached US and UK for military help.

nodes.label: Bandung Conference (1955)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Afro-Asian conference held in Bandung, Indonesia in 1955. Marked the zenith of India's engagement with newly independent Asian and African nations. Later led to the establishment of the Non-Aligned Movement. India was a key participant under Nehru's leadership.

nodes.label: Indo-Pakistan War (1965)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Pakistan launched armed attacks in Rann of Kutch (April 1965) followed by a bigger offensive in J&K (August-September). PM Shastri ordered counter-offensive on Punjab border; Indian army reached close to Lahore. Ended with Tashkent Agreement brokered by USSR in January 1966.

nodes.label: Bangladesh War (1971)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: India intervened in East Pakistan after Pakistani army's crackdown on Bengali population. About 80 lakh refugees fled to India. India signed Treaty of Peace and Friendship with USSR. War lasted 13 days; 90,000 Pakistani soldiers surrendered. Bangladesh was created. Shimla Agreement signed July 1972.

nodes.label: Tashkent Agreement (1966)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Peace agreement between India (PM Shastri) and Pakistan (Gen Ayub Khan) brokered by Soviet Union to end the 1965 war. Signed in January 1966. PM Shastri died in Tashkent immediately after signing the agreement, leading to the second succession crisis in India.

nodes.label: India's First Nuclear Test (1974)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: India conducted its first nuclear explosion in May 1974 at Pokhran, termed a 'peaceful explosion'. India's nuclear programme was initiated in the late 1940s under Homi J. Bhabha. India opposed the NPT of 1968 as discriminatory. The test came during a period of domestic economic crisis.

nodes.label: Tibet and Dalai Lama
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: China took control of Tibet in 1950. India conceded China's claim over Tibet through Panchsheel (1954). In 1959, after armed uprising against Chinese occupation, the Dalai Lama fled to India and was granted asylum. This strained India-China relations and contributed to the 1962 war.

nodes.label: Indo-Soviet Treaty of Friendship (1971)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: 20-year Treaty of Peace and Friendship signed with the Soviet Union in August 1971, to counter the US-Pakistan-China axis before the Bangladesh war. Assured India of Soviet support against attack. Questioned India's non-aligned credentials but was seen as strategic necessity.

nodes.label: Lal Bahadur Shastri as PM
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: PM from 1964 to 1966 after Nehru's death. Known for simplicity and principles -- had earlier resigned as Railway Minister accepting moral responsibility for a railway accident. Coined the slogan 'Jai Jawan Jai Kisan'. Led India through the 1965 war with Pakistan. Died in Tashkent in January 1966.
nodes.chapter_title: Challenges to and Restoration of the Congress System

nodes.label: Rise of Indira Gandhi
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Became PM in 1966 after defeating Morarji Desai in a secret ballot among Congress MPs. Daughter of Nehru but initially seen as a political novice. Senior leaders (the Syndicate) backed her expecting she would be pliable. She gradually asserted independence and sidelined the old guard.
nodes.chapter_title: Challenges to and Restoration of the Congress System

nodes.label: Fourth General Elections (1967)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: A landmark election described as a 'political earthquake'. Congress won Lok Sabha with its lowest tally since 1952. Lost power in 9 states including UP, Bihar, Punjab, West Bengal, Kerala. DMK won Tamil Nadu with a clear majority -- first non-Congress party to do so. Marked the beginning of coalition politics.
nodes.chapter_title: Challenges to and Restoration of the Congress System

nodes.label: Congress Split (1969)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Indira Gandhi's conflict with the Syndicate came to a head during the 1969 Presidential election. Indira supported V.V. Giri against the Syndicate's candidate Sanjeeva Reddy. Congress split into Congress(R) led by Indira and Congress(O) led by the Syndicate. Indira projected it as a socialist vs conservative divide.
nodes.chapter_title: Challenges to and Restoration of the Congress System

nodes.label: 1971 Lok Sabha Election
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Congress(R)-CPI alliance won 375 seats (Congress(R) alone won 352) with 48.4% votes. The Grand Alliance of opposition parties (SSP, PSP, Jana Sangh, Swatantra, BKD) was a grand failure with less than 40 seats combined. Congress(O) won only 16 seats. Restored Congress dominance under Indira.
nodes.chapter_title: Challenges to and Restoration of the Congress System

nodes.label: Bank Nationalisation (1969)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Indira Gandhi nationalised 14 leading private banks in July 1969 as part of her Left-oriented policy push. This was a popular move that gave the government control over credit allocation. It was part of her strategy to build independence from the Syndicate and demonstrate socialist credentials.
nodes.chapter_title: Challenges to and Restoration of the Congress System

nodes.label: Abolition of Privy Purse
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Privy purse was the government allowance given to former princely rulers after integration. Indira Gandhi pushed for abolition as it contradicted constitutional principles of equality. First attempt failed in Rajya Sabha and was struck down by Supreme Court. Succeeded through constitutional amendment after 1971 election victory.
nodes.chapter_title: Challenges to and Restoration of the Congress System

nodes.label: Rupee Devaluation (1966)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: One of Indira Gandhi's first decisions as PM was to devalue the Indian rupee under pressure from the US. Dollar price went from less than Rs 5 to more than Rs 7. Added to economic difficulties and public resentment. Was a politically unpopular move.
nodes.chapter_title: Challenges to and Restoration of the Congress System

nodes.label: K. Kamraj
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Congress President and former Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu. Leader of the Syndicate. Proposed the 'Kamraj Plan' in 1963 where senior Congressmen should resign from office to make way for younger workers. Played kingmaker role in choosing both Shastri and Indira as PM.
nodes.chapter_title: Challenges to and Restoration of the Congress System

nodes.label: Morarji Desai
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Former Chief Minister of Bombay state and Indira's main rival. Deputy PM and Finance Minister but left after differences over bank nationalisation. Led Congress(O) after the split. Later became PM heading the Janata Party government in 1977.
nodes.chapter_title: Challenges to and Restoration of the Congress System

nodes.label: Ten Point Programme (1967)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Adopted by the Congress Working Committee in May 1967 at Indira Gandhi's initiative. Included social control of banks, nationalisation of general insurance, ceiling on urban property and income, public distribution of food grains, land reforms. Gave government policy a Left orientation.
nodes.chapter_title: Challenges to and Restoration of the Congress System

nodes.label: Emergency (1975-77)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: On 25 June 1975, PM Indira Gandhi declared internal Emergency under Article 352 on grounds of internal disturbances. Fundamental Rights suspended, press censored, opposition leaders arrested, RSS and Jamaat-e-Islami banned. About 1 lakh 11 thousand arrested under preventive detention. Lasted 18 months.

nodes.label: JP Movement (Total Revolution)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: In 1974, students in Bihar invited Jayaprakash Narayan to lead their movement against rising prices, corruption and unemployment. JP demanded dismissal of Bihar government and called for 'Total Revolution' (Sampoorna Kranti). In 1975, he led a massive peoples march to Parliament and asked army/police to disobey illegal orders.

nodes.label: Jayaprakash Narayan (JP)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Marxist in youth, founder of Congress Socialist Party, hero of 1942 Quit India movement. Declined to join Nehru's cabinet. After 1955, became Gandhian involved in Bhoodan movement. Led Bihar movement in 1974, became symbol of opposition to Emergency, and was the moving force behind the Janata Party.

nodes.label: Allahabad High Court Verdict (1975)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: On 12 June 1975, Justice Jagmohan Lal Sinha declared Indira Gandhi's election to Lok Sabha invalid on a petition by Raj Narain. She was found to have used government servants in her campaign. Supreme Court granted partial stay. This verdict was the immediate trigger for the declaration of Emergency.

nodes.label: Naxalite Movement
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Began in 1967 with peasant uprising in Naxalbari (Darjeeling, West Bengal). CPI(ML) formed in 1969 under Charu Majumdar. Argued Indian democracy was a sham and adopted strategy of protracted guerrilla warfare. Spread to many states. About 75 districts in 9 states affected by Naxalite violence.

nodes.label: Railway Strike (1974)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: National strike by railway employees led by George Fernandes demanding bonus and better service conditions. Government declared it illegal, arrested leaders, deployed territorial army. Strike called off after 20 days without settlement. Added to atmosphere of labour unrest before Emergency.

nodes.label: Gujarat Movement (1974)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Student agitation in January 1974 against rising prices of food and cooking oil, and corruption. Joined by opposition parties. Led to President's Rule in Gujarat. Morarji Desai went on indefinite fast demanding fresh elections. Congress was defeated in the subsequent Gujarat election in June 1975.

nodes.label: Janata Party
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Formed in 1977 by merging opposition parties (Congress(O), Jana Sangh, BLD, Socialist Party) under JP's leadership for the post-Emergency elections. Won 330 seats in 1977 election, defeating Congress (154 seats). Morarji Desai became PM. Government collapsed in 1979 due to internal contradictions.

nodes.label: 1977 Lok Sabha Election
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: First election after Emergency, treated as a referendum on Emergency. Janata Party won decisively. Congress party defeated for the first time since independence -- won only 154 seats with less than 35% vote share. Indira Gandhi herself lost her seat. Demonstrated that anti-democratic governments will be punished by voters.

nodes.label: Shah Commission of Inquiry
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Appointed by Janata government in May 1977 under Justice J.C. Shah (retired CJI) to inquire into excesses during Emergency. Found widespread abuse of authority. Indira Gandhi appeared but refused to answer questions. Reports were tabled in Parliament.

nodes.label: Press Censorship During Emergency
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Government disconnected electricity to newspaper offices, imposed prior approval for all publications. Indian Express and Statesman protested by leaving blank spaces. Magazines Seminar and Mainstream chose to shut down. Many journalists arrested. Kannada writer Karanth and Hindi writer Renu returned Padma awards in protest.

nodes.label: ADM Jabalpur Case (Habeas Corpus)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: In April 1976, the Supreme Court constitution bench overruled High Courts and accepted the government's plea that during Emergency, courts cannot entertain habeas corpus petitions. Meant government could take away right to life and liberty. Regarded as one of the most controversial SC judgments.

nodes.label: 44th Constitutional Amendment (1978)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Passed by Janata government to undo Emergency-era changes. Internal Emergency can now be proclaimed only on grounds of 'armed rebellion' (not internal disturbances). Advice to President must be given in writing by Cabinet. Right to life and liberty cannot be suspended even during Emergency.

nodes.label: Forced Sterilisation and Demolitions
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: During Emergency, Sanjay Gandhi (PM's son, holding no official position) allegedly controlled administration. Over-enthusiasm about population control led to compulsory sterilisation. Turkman Gate area in Delhi saw forced demolitions and sterilisations. These excesses became symbols of Emergency abuse.

nodes.label: Chipko Movement
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Environmental movement that began in 1973 in Uttarakhand when villagers hugged trees to prevent commercial logging. Started when forest dept refused villagers ash trees for tools but allotted the same land to a sports manufacturer. Led to a 15-year ban on felling trees in the Himalayan regions. Women's active participation was a novel aspect.

nodes.label: Dalit Panthers
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Militant organisation of Dalit youth formed in Maharashtra in 1972. Fought against caste-based inequalities and atrocities despite constitutional guarantees. Broader agenda was to destroy caste system and unite all oppressed sections. Contributed to the passage of a comprehensive law against Dalit atrocities in 1989.

nodes.label: Bharatiya Kisan Union (BKU)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Farmers organisation from western UP and Haryana. In January 1988, 20,000 farmers gathered in Meerut protesting electricity rate hike. Demanded higher floor prices for sugarcane and wheat, abolition of restrictions on farm produce movement, loan waivers, and pensions. Used caste panchayat networks for mobilisation.

nodes.label: Narmada Bachao Andolan
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Movement against the Sardar Sarovar Dam on river Narmada, led by Medha Patkar. Raised fundamental questions about large dam projects, displacement of tribal communities, environmental destruction and the meaning of development. Became a symbol of peoples resistance against state-driven development.

nodes.label: BAMCEF
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Backward and Minority Communities Employees Federation formed in 1978. Not an ordinary trade union -- took strong position in favour of political power to the 'bahujan' (SC, ST, OBC and minorities). Led by Kanshi Ram. Precursor organisation to the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP).

nodes.label: Right to Information Movement
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Movement demanding transparency in governance. Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan (MKSS) in Rajasthan pioneered the demand for the right to information about government expenditure. Eventually led to the Right to Information Act, 2005.

nodes.label: Shetkari Sanghatana
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Maharashtra-based farmers organisation that declared the farmers movement as a war of Bharat (rural, agrarian sector) against India (urban, industrial sector). Along with BKU, represented the farmers movement of the 1980s against liberalisation policies.

nodes.label: SC/ST Prevention of Atrocities Act (1989)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Comprehensive law passed in 1989 providing rigorous punishment for atrocities against Dalits. Result of sustained agitations by Dalit Panthers and other organisations. Despite constitutional abolition of untouchability, social discrimination and violence against Dalits continued to necessitate this law.

nodes.label: Telangana Peasant Movement
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Massive agitations by peasants in the Telangana region of Andhra Pradesh under Communist party leadership in the early years of independence. Demanded redistribution of land to cultivators. One of the earliest post-independence social movements linking land reforms to political power.

nodes.label: Medha Patkar
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Social activist who led the Narmada Bachao Andolan against the Sardar Sarovar Dam. Raised issues of displacement, rehabilitation of tribals, and environmental sustainability. Became a prominent face of peoples movements challenging the dominant development model.

nodes.label: Sheikh Abdullah
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Leader of National Conference and key figure in Kashmir politics. Became PM of J&K in 1948. Initiated land reforms but dismissed in 1953 over differences with Centre on Kashmir's status and detained for years. Reached agreement with Indira Gandhi in 1974 and became Chief Minister.

nodes.label: Kashmir Insurgency (1989)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: By 1989, militant movement mobilised around separate Kashmiri nation. Triggered by rigged 1987 elections and growing resentment against Centre's interference. Insurgents got support from Pakistan. State under President's rule and armed forces control through the 1990s. Assembly elections held only in 1996.

nodes.label: Punjab Crisis
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: In the 1980s, demand for Sikh political autonomy escalated from the Anandpur Sahib Resolution (1973) to extremist demands for Khalistan. Militants made headquarters in Golden Temple. Led to Operation Blue Star, Indira Gandhi's assassination, anti-Sikh riots, and a decade of militancy.

nodes.label: Anandpur Sahib Resolution (1973)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Resolution passed at Akali Dal conference asserting regional autonomy and redefining centre-state relations. Spoke of aspirations of the Sikh qaum and declared goal of attaining 'bolbala' (dominance). Could be interpreted as plea for federalism or for separate Sikh nation.

nodes.label: Operation Blue Star (1984)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Army action in the Golden Temple, Amritsar in June 1984 to flush out militants. Government successfully removed militants but damaged the historic temple, deeply hurting Sikh sentiments. A large proportion of Sikhs saw it as an attack on their faith. Gave further impetus to extremism.

nodes.label: Assassination of Indira Gandhi (1984)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: PM Indira Gandhi was assassinated on 31 October 1984 by her Sikh bodyguards wanting revenge for Operation Blue Star. Followed by organised anti-Sikh violence -- over 2000 Sikhs killed in Delhi alone, hundreds in other parts of India. PM Manmohan Singh apologised in Parliament in 2005.

nodes.label: Punjab Accord (Rajiv-Longowal, 1985)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Agreement between PM Rajiv Gandhi and Akali Dal president Harchand Singh Longowal in July 1985. Chandigarh to be transferred to Punjab, commission for border dispute, tribunal for river water sharing, compensation for militancy victims, withdrawal of AFSPA. Longowal was assassinated shortly after.

nodes.label: Dravidian Movement
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: One of the first regional movements in Indian politics. Led to formation of Dravida Kazhagam (DK) under E.V. Ramasami Periyar. Opposed Brahmin dominance and north Indian cultural domination. DMK formed as political offshoot, came to power in 1967. Split into DMK and AIADMK. Good example of compatibility of regionalism and nationalism.

nodes.label: Anti-Hindi Agitation
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Protests in Tamil Nadu against making Hindi the official national language, especially intense in 1965. Led by DMK and students. Added greatly to DMK's popularity and contributed to its victory in 1967 elections. Forced the central government to continue English alongside Hindi.

nodes.label: Mizo Accord (1986)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Peace accord signed between PM Rajiv Gandhi and MNF leader Laldenga in 1986. Mizoram became a full state in 1987. The MNF came to power through democratic elections. Regarded as one of the most successful peace accords in Indian history. Ended two decades of insurgency.

nodes.label: Assam Movement (1979-85)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Anti-foreigners movement led by All Assam Students Union (AASU) demanding identification and deportation of illegal immigrants, mainly from Bangladesh. Led to Assam Accord of 1985 with PM Rajiv Gandhi. AASU leaders formed Asom Gana Parishad and won state elections.

nodes.label: Mandal Commission
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Second Backward Classes Commission chaired by B.P. Mandal, set up in 1978. Recommended 27% reservation in central government jobs and educational institutions for Other Backward Classes (OBCs). Submitted report in 1980. Implementation by V.P. Singh government in 1990 triggered violent anti-Mandal protests.

nodes.label: Implementation of Mandal Commission (1990)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: National Front government under PM V.P. Singh decided in August 1990 to implement Mandal Commission recommendations for OBC reservations. Triggered violent protests, self-immolations. Supreme Court upheld in the Indira Sawhney case (1992). All major parties now support OBC reservations. Reshaped Indian politics around caste identity.

nodes.label: Shah Bano Case (1985)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: 62-year-old divorced Muslim woman won Supreme Court ruling for maintenance from ex-husband. Orthodox Muslims opposed it as interference in Muslim Personal Law. Congress government passed Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Divorce) Act 1986 nullifying the SC judgment. BJP criticised this as 'appeasement' of minorities.

nodes.label: Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Founded by Kanshi Ram in 1984 out of BAMCEF and DS-4. Envisaged as organisation based on pragmatic politics for bahujans (SC, ST, OBC and minorities). First major breakthrough in UP in 1989-91 elections. Under Mayawati, governed UP multiple times. First party primarily supported by Dalit voters to achieve such political success.

nodes.label: V.P. Singh
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: PM from 1989-90 heading the National Front government with outside support from BJP and Left. Former Congress leader who broke away. His decision to implement Mandal Commission recommendations transformed Indian politics. Government fell when BJP withdrew support over the Ayodhya issue.

nodes.label: Kanshi Ram
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Proponent of Bahujan empowerment. Left central government job for political work. Founded BAMCEF, DS-4 and BSP (1984). Regarded political power as the master key to social equality. Astute political strategist credited with Dalit resurgence in north Indian states.

nodes.label: Courts
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Part of the government that resolves disputes and handles crimes. If a person feels that laws are not being followed (e.g., denied a job due to religion or caste), they can approach the court, which can give orders about what should be done.

nodes.label: Hindu Succession Amendment Act 2005
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: A law that gave Hindu women equal right to inherit family agricultural land. Previously, in some states, only sons inherited agricultural property. Under the new law, sons, daughters, and mothers get equal shares. Applies to all states and union territories.

nodes.label: Indian Judiciary
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: The system of courts enforcing rule of law, resolving disputes, conducting judicial review, and protecting Fundamental Rights. An independent organ of government and key feature of Indian democracy. Serves as check on legislature and executive.

nodes.label: Subordinate/District Courts
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Lowest tier at district or tehsil level. Known as Trial Court, District Judge Court, Sessions Court, Magistrate Court etc. Each district presided by a District Judge. Most people interact with these courts.

nodes.label: Olga Tellis vs Bombay Municipal Corporation (1985)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Landmark Supreme Court judgment establishing Right to Livelihood as part of Right to Life under Article 21. Court held that eviction of slum dwellers deprives them of livelihood and consequently of life. No person can live without means of living.

nodes.label: Bhopal Gas Tragedy
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: The world's worst industrial tragedy on 2 December 1984. MIC gas leaked from Union Carbide's pesticide factory in Bhopal. Over 8,000 died within three days, hundreds of thousands maimed. UC had deliberately ignored safety measures to cut costs. Government filed $3 billion case but accepted only $470 million in 1989.

nodes.label: Subhash Kumar vs State of Bihar (1991)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Supreme Court held that the Right to Life under Article 21 includes the right to enjoyment of pollution-free water and air for full enjoyment of life. Government is responsible for setting up laws and procedures to check pollution and introduce heavy fines.

nodes.label: Salvador Allende (Chile)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Democratically elected socialist President of Chile (1970-1973). Implemented land redistribution, free milk for children, and education reforms. Overthrown and killed in military coup on 11 September 1973 led by General Pinochet.

nodes.label: Pinochet's Military Dictatorship
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: General Augusto Pinochet ruled Chile from 1973-1990 after a US-supported military coup. Over 3,000 people killed, many more disappeared. Dictatorship ended after 1988 referendum where people voted no to his continued rule.

nodes.label: Solidarity Movement (Poland)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: First independent trade union in any communist state, formed in 1980 at Gdansk shipyard. Led by Lech Walesa, grew to one crore members. Won 99 of 100 Senate seats in 1989 free elections, leading to Poland's democratic transition.

nodes.label: Lech Walesa
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Former electrician who led the Solidarity trade union movement in Poland. Emerged as leader of striking workers at Gdansk shipyard in 1980. Elected President of Poland in 1990 after democratic transition.

nodes.label: Decolonisation and Democracy
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: After World War II, many colonies gained independence and adopted democratic governments. Many countries in Asia and Africa became democratic between 1950-1975, significantly expanding democracy's global reach.

nodes.label: Constituent Assembly of India
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Formed in 1946, had 299 members elected by existing provincial legislatures. Chaired by Dr. Rajendra Prasad. Drafting Committee headed by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar. Worked for 2 years 11 months 18 days. Constitution adopted on 26 November 1949, enacted on 26 January 1950.

nodes.label: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Indian Constitution. Champion of Dalit rights, legal luminary who studied at Columbia and London. Played the most important role in drafting the Constitution. Also India's first Law Minister.

nodes.label: Parliament of India
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Supreme legislative body consisting of President and two Houses - Lok Sabha (House of the People) and Rajya Sabha (Council of States). Final authority for making laws, controls government finances, and is highest forum for public debate.

nodes.label: President of India
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Head of state and highest formal authority. Elected indirectly by an electoral college. Exercises powers on advice of Council of Ministers. Appoints PM, gives assent to bills, can return bills for reconsideration. Nominal executive head.

nodes.label: Judiciary of India
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Independent branch that settles disputes and protects fundamental rights. Supreme Court at apex, High Courts at state level, subordinate courts below. Can declare laws unconstitutional (judicial review). Integrated and independent judiciary.

nodes.label: Kosovo Ethnic Massacre
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: In Kosovo province of Yugoslavia, Serb nationalist Milosevic's government persecuted ethnic Albanians despite being democratically elected. Thousands killed in ethnic cleansing. Shows that even elected governments can violate rights if unchecked.

nodes.label: National Human Rights Commission (NHRC)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Statutory body established to protect and promote human rights in India. Investigates complaints of human rights violations. Can recommend compensation and action against violators. Works alongside judiciary in rights protection.

nodes.label: Consumer Movement in India
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Originated as a social force to protect consumers against unethical trade practices. Triggered by food shortages, hoarding, black marketing, adulteration in 1960s. Early activities: articles, exhibitions, monitoring ration shops. Led to COPRA 1986. Over 700 consumer groups in India but only 20-25 well organised.

nodes.label: Consumer Protection Act 1986 (COPRA)
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Enacted on 24 December 1986 (celebrated as National Consumers' Day). Major step by Indian government for consumer protection. Set up three-tier quasi-judicial machinery for consumer disputes redressal. Led to separate Consumer Affairs departments in central and state governments. India has exclusive consumer courts.

nodes.label: UN Guidelines for Consumer Protection
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Adopted by United Nations in 1985. A tool for nations to adopt consumer protection measures. Foundation for international consumer movement. Consumers International: umbrella body of 240 organisations from over 100 countries. India observes 24 December as National Consumers' Day.

nodes.label: Planning Commission
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Set up in 1950 with the Prime Minister as Chairperson to formulate five year plans. India chose a mixed economy model combining features of socialism and capitalism. The era of five year plans became the basis for India's planned development from 1950 to 2017 when NITI Aayog replaced it.

nodes.label: Five Year Plans
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Borrowed from the Soviet Union, these plans specified objectives for five-year periods within a twenty-year perspective plan. The four key goals were growth (increase in GDP), modernisation (new technology adoption), self-reliance (reducing import dependence), and equity (basic needs for all).

nodes.label: P.C. Mahalanobis
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Statistician regarded as the architect of Indian planning. The Second Five Year Plan was based on his ideas, emphasising heavy industry and capital goods. Founded the Indian Statistical Institute (ISI) in Calcutta and the journal Sankhya. Made Fellow of Britain's Royal Society in 1946.

nodes.label: Land Reforms
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Two major components: abolition of intermediaries (zamindars, jagirdars) making tillers the owners, and land ceiling (fixing maximum land size per individual). About 200 lakh tenants came into direct contact with government. Successful in Kerala and West Bengal but largely failed elsewhere due to loopholes exploited by landlords.

nodes.label: Abolition of Zamindari
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Steps taken just a year after independence to abolish intermediaries and make tillers the owners of land. About 200 lakh tenants freed from zamindari exploitation. However, many zamindars used loopholes to retain land by registering in relatives' names. Poorest agricultural labourers did not benefit.

nodes.label: Land Ceiling
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Policy of fixing maximum size of land that could be owned by an individual to reduce concentration of land ownership. Big landlords challenged legislation in courts, used delays to register lands in relatives' names. Vast inequality in landholding continues despite this policy.

nodes.label: Green Revolution
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Large increase in food grain production through High Yielding Variety (HYV) seeds, especially wheat and rice. First phase (mid-1960s to mid-1970s) limited to affluent states like Punjab, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and mainly wheat. Second phase (mid-1970s to mid-1980s) spread wider. Made India self-sufficient in food grains.

nodes.label: Industrial Policy Resolution 1956
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Classified industries into three categories: exclusively state-owned (strategic), state-led with private supplementation, and private sector. Formed basis of Second Five Year Plan for socialist pattern of society. Private sector controlled through licensing system -- no new industry without government permission.

nodes.label: Small-Scale Industry Policy
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Karve Committee (1955) recommended using small-scale industries for rural development. Defined by maximum investment on assets (Rs 5 lakh in 1950, Rs 1 crore later). More labour-intensive than large firms, generating more employment. Given concessions: reserved products, lower excise duty, subsidised bank loans.

nodes.label: Import Substitution Policy
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Inward-looking trade strategy followed in the first seven plans, aiming to replace imports with domestic production. Protection through tariffs (tax on imports) and quotas (quantity restrictions on imports). Based on the notion that developing country industries cannot compete with developed economies without protection.

nodes.label: Second Five Year Plan (1956-61)
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Landmark plan based on Mahalanobis model emphasising heavy industry and building a socialist pattern of society. Classified industries into three categories through IPR 1956. Laid down the basic ideas regarding goals of Indian planning. Stressed that benefits of development must reach less privileged classes.

nodes.label: General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT)
nodes.subject: economics
