nodes.detail: Established in 1948 with 23 countries as the global trade organisation to administer multilateral trade agreements and provide equal opportunities to all countries in international markets. Succeeded by the WTO in 1995.
nodes.chapter_title: Liberalisation, Privatisation and Globalisation: An Appraisal

nodes.label: Growth-Oriented Approach to Poverty
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: First dimension of poverty alleviation (1950s-60s). Based on expectation that economic growth (rapid GDP increase) would trickle down to all sections. Focus on rapid industrialisation and Green Revolution. Failed because benefits did not trickle down; gap between poor and rich widened; Green Revolution exacerbated regional disparities.

nodes.label: Poverty Alleviation Programmes
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Second approach from Third Five Year Plan (1961-66). Specific programmes to raise incomes and employment for the poor through asset creation and work generation. Includes self-employment programmes (REGP, PMRY, SJSRY, SGSY) and wage employment programmes (NFWP, SGRY, NREGA-2005). Food for Work initiated in 1970s.

nodes.label: Self-Employment Programmes
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Include REGP (rural/small town self-employment via Khadi and Village Industries Commission), PMRY (educated unemployed from low-income families), SJSRY (urban employment), and SGSY (self-help group based). Since 1990s, approach shifted from individual assistance to encouraging Self-Help Groups (SHGs).

nodes.label: Minimum Basic Amenities Approach
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Third approach from Fifth Five Year Plan. India pioneered public expenditure on social consumption -- subsidised food grains, education, health, water, sanitation. Key programmes: PDS, ICDS, Midday Meal Scheme, PMGSY, PMGY, Valmiki Ambedkar Awas Yojana. Aims to supplement consumption and improve health/education of the poor.

nodes.label: Public Distribution System (PDS)
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Major programme providing food grains at subsidised rates to the poor. One of three key programmes along with ICDS and Midday Meal aimed at improving food and nutritional status of the poor. Part of the minimum basic amenities approach to poverty alleviation.

nodes.label: National Social Assistance Programme
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Central government social security programme providing pensions to elderly without caregivers and assistance to destitute and widowed poor women. Part of the government's variety of social security programmes targeting specific vulnerable groups.

nodes.label: Education Commission (1964-66)
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Recommended that at least 6% of GDP should be spent on education for noticeable growth in educational achievements. More than 40 years later, India's education spending was still around 4%, well short of this target. The 6% goal has been accepted as a must for coming years.

nodes.label: NABARD (National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development)
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Set up in 1982 as apex body to coordinate activities of all institutions involved in rural financing. Green Revolution diversified rural credit portfolio towards production-oriented lending. NABARD oversees the multi-agency rural banking system comprising commercial banks, RRBs, cooperatives, and land development banks.

nodes.label: Regulated Markets
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: First step in agricultural marketing reform: creating orderly and transparent marketing conditions. Benefited farmers and consumers. However, about 27,000 rural periodic markets still need development as regulated market places to realise the full potential of rural markets.

nodes.label: MSP, Buffer Stock and PDS
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Fourth element of agricultural marketing: (i) Minimum Support Prices for 24 agricultural products protecting farmer income, (ii) Buffer stocks of wheat and rice maintained by Food Corporation of India, (iii) Distribution of food grains and sugar through PDS at subsidised rates. Despite this, private trade handles 90% of agricultural marketing.

nodes.label: Operation Flood
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Launched from 1966 onwards, it created a system where farmers pool milk by quality grading, which is processed and marketed to urban centres through cooperatives. Farmers assured fair price and income. Gujarat is the success story. Milk production in India increased more than four times between 1960-2002.

nodes.label: Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Set up in 1974 to address water and air pollution. State-level boards followed. Functions: investigate and disseminate information on pollution, set standards for sewage/emissions, provide technical assistance, organise mass awareness, prepare manuals for waste disposal, assess air quality, monitor water quality in 125 rivers. Industries periodically inspected.

nodes.label: Chipko and Appiko Movements
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Chipko Movement aimed at protecting Himalayan forests. Appiko Movement in Karnataka (1983) -- 160 people in Salkani forest, Sirsi district hugged trees to stop commercial felling, saving 12,000 trees. Spread to adjoining districts. Demonstrated how community action can protect forests from indiscriminate commercial exploitation.

nodes.label: Great Leap Forward (GLF)
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Campaign initiated in 1958 to industrialise China on a massive scale. People encouraged to set up industries in backyards. In rural areas, communes were started for collective cultivation. Met many problems: severe drought killed about 30 million people. Russia withdrew its professionals after conflicts with China.
nodes.chapter_title: Comparative Development Experiences of India and Its Neighbours

nodes.label: Commune System in China
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Under the Great Leap Forward, people collectively cultivated lands in communes. By 1958, there were 26,000 communes covering almost all the farm population. During 1978 reforms, commune lands were divided into small plots allocated to individual households (for use, not ownership). Households kept income after paying stipulated taxes.
nodes.chapter_title: Comparative Development Experiences of India and Its Neighbours

nodes.label: Great Proletarian Cultural Revolution
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Introduced by Mao in 1965, implemented 1966-76. Students and professionals were sent to work and learn from the countryside. A political movement that disrupted education and professional development in China. Pre-dated the economic reforms that began in 1978.
nodes.chapter_title: Comparative Development Experiences of India and Its Neighbours

nodes.label: China's 1978 Economic Reforms
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Introduced in phases. First phase: agriculture (commune lands to individual households), foreign trade, and investment reforms. Later phase: industrial reforms with private sector and township/village enterprises allowed. SOEs (State Owned Enterprises) faced competition. Dual pricing system: government-fixed prices for fixed quantities, market prices for the rest.
nodes.chapter_title: Comparative Development Experiences of India and Its Neighbours

nodes.label: Special Economic Zones (China)
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Set up to attract foreign investors as part of China's reform process. Along with township and village enterprises, SEZs became key drivers of China's export-oriented industrial growth. These zones offered special incentives and regulations different from the rest of the economy.
nodes.chapter_title: Comparative Development Experiences of India and Its Neighbours

nodes.label: Dual Pricing System (China)
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Reform process involved fixing prices in two ways: farmers and industrial units bought/sold fixed quantities at government-set prices, with the rest at market prices. Over time, as production increased, the proportion transacted at market prices was gradually increased.
nodes.chapter_title: Comparative Development Experiences of India and Its Neighbours

nodes.label: Pakistan's Green Revolution
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Led to mechanisation and increase in public investment in infrastructure in select areas, resulting in rise in food grain production. Changed the agrarian structure dramatically. Similar to India's experience but with different scale and outcomes.
nodes.chapter_title: Comparative Development Experiences of India and Its Neighbours

nodes.label: China's One-Child Policy
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Introduced in late 1970s, major reason for China's low population growth rate. Led to decline in sex ratio (proportion of females per 1000 males) -- biased against females due to son-preference. Has implications for future ageing population, rising labour costs, and potential labour shortage.
nodes.chapter_title: Comparative Development Experiences of India and Its Neighbours

nodes.label: SAARC and Regional Groupings
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation. Nations form regional and global economic groupings (SAARC, EU, ASEAN, G-8, G-20) to strengthen domestic economies. Understanding neighbouring economies is essential as developing countries face competition from each other and from developed nations in limited economic space.
nodes.chapter_title: Comparative Development Experiences of India and Its Neighbours

nodes.label: Bengal Famine of 1943
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Most devastating famine in India, killed 30 lakh people in Bengal. Agricultural labourers, fishermen, transport workers, and casual labourers were worst affected by dramatically rising rice prices. Led to the introduction of rationing system in India.

nodes.label: National Food Security Act (2013)
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Provides food and nutritional security at affordable prices. Covers 75% of rural population and 50% of urban population as eligible households. Entitles 5 kg per person per month at Rs 2/kg wheat, Rs 3/kg rice, Rs 1/kg coarse grains.

nodes.label: Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS)
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Introduced in 1975 on experimental basis as a food intervention programme. Along with PDS and Food-for-Work (1977-78), one of three major food security interventions launched in mid-1970s following high poverty levels reported by NSSO.

nodes.label: Battle of Dien Bien Phu
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: In 1954 French forces decisively defeated by Viet Minh at Dien Bien Phu. This ended French colonial rule in Indo-China. Led to Geneva Peace Agreement dividing Vietnam at 17th parallel.

nodes.label: Vietnam War (US Involvement)
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: US entered to prevent communist takeover of South Vietnam. Used napalm and Agent Orange extensively. First television war created anti-war movement in US. Peace signed in Paris 1974. Saigon fell 30 April 1975.

nodes.label: Ho Chi Minh Trail
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Network of paths through Laos and Cambodia used to transport supplies to South Vietnam. 2,195 km of strategic roads maintained by young volunteers, 70-80% women. Vital supply line despite constant US bombing.

nodes.label: Ngo Dinh Diem
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: US-backed dictator of South Vietnam. Built authoritarian government, refused land reform. His brutal suppression of Buddhists and political opponents ultimately lost US support. Overthrown and killed in 1963 coup.

nodes.label: Formation of Linguistic States
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Potti Sriramulu's death after 58-day fast in 1952 forced creation of Andhra state in 1953. States Reorganisation Commission (1956) redrew boundaries for linguistic provinces. Bombay divided in 1960, Punjab in 1966.

nodes.label: Hindi as Official Language Debate
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Many wanted Hindi to replace English as official language. T.T. Krishnamachari warned southern states would separate if Hindi imposed. Compromise: Hindi as official language with English for courts, services and inter-state communication.

nodes.label: Ambedkar as Chairman of Drafting Committee
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: B.R. Ambedkar chaired the Constitution's Drafting Committee. Warned that political democracy must be accompanied by economic and social democracy, as equality in politics coexists with inequality in social and economic life.

nodes.label: Potti Sriramulu
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Gandhian leader who fasted unto death demanding separate state for Telugu speakers. Died on 15 December 1952 after 58 days of fasting. His death forced the creation of Andhra state on 1 October 1953.

nodes.label: Mao Zedong
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Founded People's Republic of China 1949. Peasant-based adaptation of Marxism. Long March 1934-35. Great Leap Forward 1958-62. Cultural Revolution 1966-76.

nodes.label: Chinese Communist Revolution (1949)
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Mao defeated KMT; PRC proclaimed 1 Oct 1949. Land redistribution, industry nationalised. Chiang retreated Taiwan.

nodes.label: Great Leap Forward (1958-62)
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Mao's collectivisation + backyard steel furnaces. Catastrophic famine 15-45M deaths. Mao temporarily lost standing.

nodes.label: Cultural Revolution (1966-76)
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Mao vs 'bourgeois' elements. Red Guards attacked intellectuals + traditional culture. Millions persecuted. Universities closed. Ended with Mao's death 1976.

nodes.label: Deng Xiaoping
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Paramount leader from 1978. 'Socialism with Chinese characteristics' = market reforms, Special Economic Zones. Suppressed Tiananmen 1989.

nodes.label: G-77 and NIEO
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Group of 77 developing countries demanded New International Economic Order: resource sovereignty, development aid, fairer commodity prices, market access.

nodes.label: Cold War
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Competition, tensions and confrontations between the US and Soviet Union from 1945 to 1991. Both a power rivalry and an ideological conflict between liberal democracy/capitalism and socialism/communism. Never escalated into direct full-scale war between the two superpowers.

nodes.label: Two Power Blocs
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Post-WWII world divided into Western (capitalist, US-led) and Eastern (communist, Soviet-led) alliances. Smaller states joined blocs for protection, weapons, and economic aid. Division first occurred in Europe, then extended globally.

nodes.label: Sukarno
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: First President of Indonesia (1945-65). One of five founders of NAM. Organised the Bandung Conference in 1955. Championed socialism and anti-imperialism. Overthrown in a military coup.

nodes.label: India and the Cold War
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: India pursued non-alignment, staying away from both alliances while actively mediating. Served India by allowing independent decisions and balancing superpowers. Signed Treaty of Friendship with USSR in 1971 during Bangladesh crisis.

nodes.label: Arms Race
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Competitive buildup of nuclear and conventional weapons between US and USSR. Both stockpiled thousands of thermonuclear weapons. Led to arms control treaties (SALT-I, SALT-II, START-I, START-II).

nodes.label: India-USSR Relations (Cold War Era)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Multi-dimensional relationship covering economic aid (Bhilai, Bokaro steel plants), political support (Kashmir in UN, 1971 war), military hardware supply, and cultural exchanges. USSR accepted Indian currency for trade. Led critics to call India part of the Soviet camp.

nodes.label: Marshall Plan
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: US aid programme (1947-52) for reconstruction of Western Europe. Led to the establishment of OEEC in 1948 to channel aid. Helped European economic recovery and integration. Part of the US Cold War strategy of containment.

nodes.label: Democracy in Pakistan
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Alternated between civilian and military rule. Military coups by Ayub Khan, Yahya Khan, Zia-ul-Haq, and Pervez Musharraf. Social dominance of military, clergy, and landowners undermines democracy. Pakistan joined Cold War blocs SEATO and CENTO. Strong pro-democracy sentiment exists despite military dominance.

nodes.label: India-Pakistan Conflicts
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Wars in 1947-48, 1965, 1971, and Kargil conflict 1999. Kashmir dispute remains central. Both conducted nuclear tests in 1998 (India at Pokhran, Pakistan at Chagai Hills). Disputes over Siachen glacier, Sir Creek, and cross-border terrorism. Indus Waters Treaty (1960) has survived all conflicts.

nodes.label: Kashmir Issue
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Dispute since partition in 1947. Wars in 1947-48 resulted in division along Line of Control. 1971 war did not settle the issue. India blames Pakistan for supporting militants. Strategic issues include Siachen glacier control. Shimla Agreement (1972) governs bilateral resolution.

nodes.label: United Nations (UN)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Founded in 1945 as successor to League of Nations, with 51 original members (192 by 2006). Signed at San Francisco. Objective: prevent conflict and facilitate cooperation. India joined on 30 October 1945. October 24 celebrated as UN Day.

nodes.label: UN General Assembly
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: All UN members have one vote each. Debates and discusses global issues including war, peace, and development. Overwhelming majority of members are now developing countries.

nodes.label: UN Security Council
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Five permanent members (US, Russia, UK, France, China) with veto power, and ten non-permanent members serving two-year terms. Responsible for maintaining international peace and security. Permanent members selected as most powerful after WWII.

nodes.label: UN Secretary-General
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Most visible public figure and representative head of the UN. Ban Ki-Moon (South Korea) became eighth Secretary-General on 1 January 2007. Previous holders include Dag Hammarskjold, U Thant, Kofi Annan. US has considerable influence in selection.

nodes.label: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: International organisation overseeing financial institutions and regulations. 184 member countries but unequal voting: top ten countries have 55% of votes. US alone has 17.4% voting rights. G-8 members plus Saudi Arabia and China dominate decision-making.

nodes.label: World Bank
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Created in 1945, focused on developing countries. Works on education, health, agriculture, infrastructure, and governance. Provides loans with conditions, often criticised for imposing free market reforms and setting economic agendas of poorer nations.

nodes.label: Three Challenges of Nation Building
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Independent India faced three broad challenges: (1) shaping a united nation accommodating diversity, (2) establishing democracy with constitutional governance, and (3) ensuring development and well-being of all sections, especially the poor and disadvantaged.

nodes.label: Policy of Non-Alignment
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: India's foreign policy of not joining either the US-led NATO or Soviet-led Warsaw Pact blocs during the Cold War. Advocated by Nehru to preserve sovereignty, protect territorial integrity and promote economic development. India was a co-founder of the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM) with its first summit in Belgrade (1961).

nodes.label: Cauvery Water Dispute
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: A conflict between Karnataka and Tamil Nadu over sharing of Cauvery river water. Water from Krishna Raja Sagara dam (Karnataka) and Mettur dam (Tamil Nadu) serves different regions. The central government must step in to ensure fair distribution. An example of inter-state conflict.
nodes.chapter_title: Key Elements of a Democratic Government

nodes.label: Instrument of Accession
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: The legal document through which princely states agreed to merge with India, transferring control over defence, external affairs and communications to the Government of India. Maharaja Hari Singh of Kashmir signed it in October 1947 after Pakistani tribal invasion.

nodes.label: Rajiv Gandhi
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Youngest PM of India (1984-89) after mother Indira's assassination 31 Oct 1984. Computer revolution beginning, telecom push (C-DOT, Sam Pitroda), Panchayati Raj initiative, Shah Bano reversal (Muslim Women Act 1986), Assam Accord 1985, Punjab Accord 1985 (Rajiv-Longowal), Mizo Accord 1986. Tarnished by Bofors scandal (1987). Assassinated 21 May 1991 in Sriperumbudur by LTTE suicide bomber.

nodes.label: M.S. Swaminathan
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Father of the Green Revolution in India. Agricultural scientist who led the HYV seed programme with Norman Borlaug's wheat varieties from Mexico/CIMMYT in the 1960s. Director of IARI. Later chair of National Commission on Farmers (2004-06).

nodes.label: Homi J. Bhabha
nodes.subject: science
nodes.detail: Father of Indian nuclear programme. Founded Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR) 1945 and Atomic Energy Commission 1948. First chairman of AEC. Designed three-stage nuclear programme using India's thorium reserves. Died in Air India Flight 101 crash Jan 1966.

nodes.label: Vikram Sarabhai
nodes.subject: science
nodes.detail: Father of Indian space programme. Founded Physical Research Laboratory (PRL) Ahmedabad 1947 and INCOSPAR 1962 (precursor to ISRO). Convinced Nehru of importance of space tech for developing country. Died 1971.

nodes.label: C. Subramaniam
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Union Minister for Food and Agriculture (1964-67) under Shastri and Indira. Political architect of Green Revolution — pushed HYV wheat adoption, created Agricultural Prices Commission (1965) and FCI (1965). Worked with Swaminathan.

nodes.label: Verghese Kurien
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Father of White Revolution / Operation Flood. Led Amul (Kaira District Cooperative) and National Dairy Development Board (NDDB, est. 1965). Transformed India from milk-deficit into world's largest milk producer via three-phase Operation Flood (1970-96).

nodes.label: Golaknath Case (1967)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: I.C. Golaknath vs State of Punjab 1967. SC held by 6-5 that Parliament cannot amend Fundamental Rights — reversed Sajjan Singh (1965) and Shankari Prasad (1951). Led to 24th Amendment (1971) explicitly reinstating Parliament's amending power over FRs. Overruled by Kesavananda Bharati 1973.

nodes.label: Maneka Gandhi Case (1978)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Maneka Gandhi vs Union of India 1978. SC expanded scope of Article 21 (Right to Life and Personal Liberty) — procedure established by law must be 'just, fair, and reasonable' (due process in substance). Overruled A.K. Gopalan (1950). Foundation of expansive Article 21 jurisprudence.

nodes.label: Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC)
nodes.subject: science
nodes.detail: India's premier nuclear research centre, Trombay Mumbai. Founded 1954 as Atomic Energy Establishment Trombay (AEET) by Homi Bhabha. Renamed BARC after his death 1967. Designed Apsara (first Asian research reactor, 1956), CIRUS, Dhruva. Core facility for Pokhran-I and II.

nodes.label: Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)
nodes.subject: science
nodes.detail: Established 15 Aug 1969 by Vikram Sarabhai, replacing INCOSPAR (1962). Under Department of Space from 1972. Early milestones: Aryabhata satellite (1975, with USSR), Rohini SLV-3 (1980, India's first indigenous satellite launch), INSAT-1A (1982), Chandrayaan (2008), Mangalyaan (2013).

nodes.label: Hyderabad Police Action (Operation Polo, Sept 1948)
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: 13-18 Sept 1948 Indian Army operation against Nizam Mir Osman Ali Khan's Hyderabad State which refused accession. Codenamed 'Operation Polo'. Triggered by Razakar militia violence. Ended in 5 days. Integrated Hyderabad into Indian Union. Major Patel achievement.

nodes.label: Junagadh Accession (1947-48)
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Junagadh Nawab (Muslim ruler, Hindu-majority population) acceded to Pakistan Aug 1947 despite geographic non-contiguity. Indian forces moved in, plebiscite held Feb 1948 — overwhelming vote for India. Integrated into Indian Union.

nodes.label: Goa Liberation (Operation Vijay, Dec 1961)
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Indian Army operation 17-19 Dec 1961 ending 451 years of Portuguese rule over Goa, Daman and Diu. Portugal refused to negotiate transfer. Ended Portuguese colonial presence in India. Goa became UT; full statehood 1987.

nodes.label: Pokhran-I / Smiling Buddha (1974)
nodes.subject: science
nodes.detail: India's first nuclear test, 18 May 1974 at Pokhran, Rajasthan. Codenamed 'Smiling Buddha'. Described officially as 'Peaceful Nuclear Explosion' (PNE). Made India sixth nuclear-weapons-capable state. Led to formation of Nuclear Suppliers Group (NSG) in 1975. Raja Ramanna led the team.

nodes.label: Hindu Code Bills (1955-56)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Four codification acts reforming Hindu personal law: Hindu Marriage Act (1955), Hindu Succession Act (1956), Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act (1956), Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act (1956). Originally proposed by Ambedkar 1948-51 (led to his resignation Sept 1951 when diluted). Finally passed under Nehru. Gave Hindu women divorce rights, inheritance rights.

nodes.label: Indus Waters Treaty (1960)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Signed 19 Sept 1960 between Nehru and Ayub Khan, brokered by World Bank. Divides Indus river system: India gets eastern rivers (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej), Pakistan gets western rivers (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab). Has survived three wars. India can use western rivers for non-consumptive purposes (hydro).

nodes.label: Shimla Agreement (1972)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Signed 2 July 1972 between Indira Gandhi and Zulfikar Ali Bhutto after 1971 war. Bilateralism principle — Kashmir to be resolved bilaterally, not internationalised. Converted 1971 ceasefire line into Line of Control (LoC). Pakistan agreed to recognise Bangladesh. Return of 93,000 POWs.

nodes.label: Article 356 - President's Rule
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Empowers President to impose central rule on a state if constitutional machinery fails. Used 100+ times 1950-1990, often for partisan purposes. Controversial misuses: Kerala 1959 (first, against EMS Namboodiripad communist govt), 1977 Janata dismissing Congress-ruled states, 1980 Indira dismissing non-Congress states. Restrained by S.R. Bommai case (1994).

nodes.label: Article 370 - Special Status of J&K
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Gave Jammu & Kashmir special autonomous status from 1949. Emerged from Instrument of Accession (Oct 1947) limited to defence, foreign affairs, communications. Only these subjects of Union List applied to J&K without state concurrence. Abrogated 5 Aug 2019 (era 11).

nodes.label: Akali Dal
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Sikh political party founded 1920 during Gurdwara reform movement. Key post-1947 role in Punjab politics — demand for Punjabi Suba (granted 1966), Anandpur Sahib Resolution 1973 (more state autonomy), Dharam Yudh Morcha 1982, led Punjab crisis leading to Operation Blue Star 1984 and Rajiv-Longowal Accord 1985.

nodes.label: License-Permit-Quota Raj
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Elaborate system of licenses, permits and quotas governing private industry 1951-1991. Industries (Development and Regulation) Act 1951 mandated licenses for establishment/expansion. Meant to direct investment toward Plan priorities but created corruption, delays, inefficiency. Dismantled by 1991 LPG reforms.

nodes.label: First Five Year Plan (1951-56)
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: 1 April 1951 - 31 March 1956. Based on Harrod-Domar model. Focus on agriculture and irrigation post-Partition. Major dams: Bhakra Nangal, Hirakud, Damodar Valley. Target 2.1% growth, achieved 3.6%. PM Nehru, Planning Commission under Mahalanobis framework.

nodes.label: Third Five Year Plan (1961-66)
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Aimed at self-reliant economy. Disrupted by 1962 China war, 1965 Pakistan war, 1965-66 drought. Plan failed — growth only 2.8%. Followed by Plan Holiday (1966-69) with annual plans. Devaluation of rupee June 1966.

nodes.label: Plan Holiday (1966-69)
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Three annual plans 1966-67, 1967-68, 1968-69 instead of a five-year plan. Caused by 1965 war strain, 1965-66 drought, rupee devaluation June 1966. Green Revolution launched in this period as interim strategy.

nodes.label: Fourth Five Year Plan (1969-74)
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Growth with stability and progressive self-reliance. Bank nationalisation 1969 (14 banks). Garibi Hatao slogan 1971. 1971 Bangladesh war, 1973 oil shock. Achieved 3.3% vs 5.7% target. Indira Gandhi era.

nodes.label: Fifth Five Year Plan (1974-78)
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Poverty removal (Garibi Hatao) + self-reliance. Minimum Needs Programme. Emergency years 1975-77. Terminated one year early by Janata govt March 1978. 4.8% growth.

nodes.label: Rolling Plan (1978-80)
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Janata govt's Gunnar Myrdal-inspired Rolling Plan replacing Fifth Plan's final year. Abandoned when Indira returned Jan 1980.

nodes.label: Sixth Five Year Plan (1980-85)
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Indira II, then Rajiv from 1984. Poverty alleviation + modernisation. IRDP (Integrated Rural Development), NREP. Family planning emphasis. 5.7% growth — first to exceed target.

nodes.label: Seventh Five Year Plan (1985-90)
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Rajiv Gandhi era. Food, work, productivity. Jawahar Rozgar Yojana 1989. Growing fiscal deficit, BOP crisis brewing. 6% growth. Ended with BOP crisis 1990-91 that triggered liberalisation.

nodes.label: First General Elections (1951-52)
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Oct 1951 - Feb 1952. 173 million voters (of whom 85% illiterate), world's largest democratic exercise. Sukumar Sen as first CEC. Congress swept with 364/489 LS seats, 45% vote share. Proved universal adult suffrage workable in mass-illiterate country.

nodes.label: Fazal Ali Commission / States Reorganisation Commission (1953)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Appointed Dec 1953 by Nehru after Potti Sriramulu's death forced Andhra's creation. Chair: Justice Fazal Ali. Members: H.N. Kunzru, K.M. Panikkar. Report submitted Sept 1955 rejected one-language-one-state principle but recommended reorganisation broadly on linguistic lines. Led to States Reorganisation Act 1956.

nodes.label: Andhra State Creation (Oct 1953)
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: First linguistic state formed after Potti Sriramulu's 58-day fast-unto-death (died 15 Dec 1952) galvanised Telugu demand. Separated from Madras State. Later merged with Telangana (Hyderabad State) in 1956 as Andhra Pradesh. Set precedent for linguistic reorganisation.

nodes.label: NEFA (North-East Frontier Agency, 1954)
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Created 1954 from Assam tribal areas. Administered by Ministry of External Affairs (not Home) under special Governor-via-President arrangement. Verrier Elwin's tribal-friendly policy. Became Arunachal Pradesh UT in 1972, state in 1987.

nodes.label: Naga Insurgency (1950s onwards)
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Led by A.Z. Phizo's Naga National Council demanding independent Nagaland. Armed rebellion from 1955. Nagaland state created 1963 (from Assam). 1975 Shillong Accord briefly held. Ongoing insurgency across decades.

nodes.label: Nehru's Tribal Policy (Panchsheel of Tribals)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Five principles articulated by Nehru (influenced by Verrier Elwin): (1) develop along lines of own genius, (2) respect tribal rights in land and forests, (3) train own team of administrators, (4) not over-administer or introduce too many outside schemes, (5) judge results by quality of human character evolved.

nodes.label: Verrier Elwin
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: British-Indian anthropologist (1902-1964), Gandhian, tribal expert. Key advisor to Nehru on tribal policy, particularly NEFA. Advocated gradualist, protective approach to tribal integration. First Indian citizen of British origin (1954).

nodes.label: Mahatma Gandhi's Assassination (30 Jan 1948)
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Shot dead at Birla House, Delhi by Nathuram Godse, former RSS/Hindu Mahasabha worker. Three bullets fired at point-blank range. Trigger: Gandhi's fasts demanding protection of Muslims and payment of Rs 55 crore to Pakistan. Led to ban on RSS (lifted 1949 after pledge). Profoundly shifted Indian politics against communalism.

nodes.label: RSS Ban (Feb 1948 - July 1949)
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh banned after Gandhi assassination in Feb 1948. Ban lifted July 1949 after RSS pledged loyalty to Constitution, flag, and renounced violence. Accepted written constitution with M.S. Golwalkar. Banned again during Emergency (1975) and after Babri (1992).

nodes.label: Princely State Mergers (Saurashtra, PEPSU, Vindhya, Madhya Bharat)
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Post-1947 consolidation: Saurashtra (1948, 222 states of Kathiawar), Madhya Bharat (1948), PEPSU (Patiala and East Punjab States Union, 1948), Vindhya Pradesh (1948), Rajasthan (1948-49). Most merged into larger states by SRC 1956.

nodes.label: Avadi Session of Congress (Jan 1955)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: 61st Congress session at Avadi, near Madras. Adopted 'Socialistic Pattern of Society' as party's declared objective. Influenced Second Five Year Plan's public-sector emphasis. Followed by Nagpur Resolution 1959 on cooperative joint farming.

nodes.label: Nagpur Resolution (Jan 1959)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Congress Nagpur session adopted 'Cooperative Joint Farming' as agrarian objective — land to be pooled into cooperatives. Created huge backlash from landed peasants. Policy effectively abandoned. Contributed to rise of Swatantra Party (1959).

nodes.label: Swatantra Party (1959)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Founded Aug 1959 by C. Rajagopalachari with N.G. Ranga, Minoo Masani. Classical liberal, anti-socialist, anti-Congress. Peak in 1967 (44 LS seats, largest opposition). Declined by 1974, formally merged into Bharatiya Kranti Dal. Key voice against licence raj.

nodes.label: Bharatiya Jana Sangh (1951)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Founded Oct 1951 by Syama Prasad Mookerjee (former Hindu Mahasabha, ex-Nehru cabinet). Aligned with RSS cadre. Anti-Congress right-wing Hindu nationalist. Under Deendayal Upadhyaya's 'Integral Humanism' (1965). Merged into Janata Party 1977; re-emerged as BJP 1980.

nodes.label: Kamaraj Plan (Aug 1963)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Devised by K. Kamaraj, then TN CM. Senior Congress leaders (6 CMs + 6 Union ministers) resigned party/govt posts to re-dedicate themselves to party organisation. Kamaraj himself resigned and became Congress President. Meant to revitalise party and ease Nehru succession. Succeeded for Nehru but unwound by 1964.

nodes.label: K. Kamaraj
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Dravidian-era Congressman, TN CM (1954-63). Created midday meal scheme and universal primary education in Tamil Nadu. Congress President (1964-67). 'Kingmaker' — engineered succession of Shastri (1964) and Indira (1966). Led Syndicate against Indira in 1969 split.

nodes.label: Congress Syndicate
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Informal group of old-guard Congress bosses: K. Kamaraj, S. Nijalingappa, S.K. Patil, Atulya Ghosh, N. Sanjiva Reddy. Dominant after Nehru's death. Backed Shastri (1964), then Indira (1966). Expelled Indira after Congress split 1969 (Congress-O vs Congress-R).

nodes.label: Mundhra Scandal (1957-58)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: First major post-independence corruption scandal. LIC purchased Rs 1.26 crore shares in Haridas Mundhra's six sank companies without board approval, under T.T. Krishnamachari's (FM) alleged direction. JP Committee inquiry. Feroze Gandhi (MP) exposed. Led to TTK's resignation Feb 1958. First LIC scandal.

nodes.label: T.T. Krishnamachari (TTK)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Congress economic thinker and Union Finance Minister (1956-58, 1964-66). Resigned 1958 over Mundhra scandal, returned as FM under Shastri. Key architect of Second Plan's industrial policy. Warned of Hindi imposition on south during Constituent Assembly.

nodes.label: V.K. Krishna Menon
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Marxist-leaning Nehru confidant, Defence Minister (1957-62). India's rep at UN, delivered record 8-hour speech on Kashmir 1957. Architect of non-alignment rhetoric. Forced to resign after 1962 China war debacle (military unpreparedness). Controversial intellectually sharp figure.

nodes.label: Feroze Gandhi
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Congress MP (Lok Sabha 1952-60), husband of Indira. Parsi journalist-politician. Rigorous backbencher — exposed Mundhra (1957) and LIC scandals. Championed PAC reforms, parliamentary accountability. Died Sept 1960.

nodes.label: Dalai Lama Takes Asylum in India (March 1959)
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: 14th Dalai Lama fled Lhasa to India after failed Tibetan uprising March 1959, reaching Tezpur 31 March. Nehru granted asylum despite Chinese protest. Established Central Tibetan Administration in Dharamshala. Key irritant souring India-China relations pre-1962 war.

nodes.label: McMahon Line
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: 1914 Simla Convention boundary between Tibet and British India along Eastern Himalayas (NEFA/Arunachal). Named after Sir Henry McMahon. China never ratified. Core of 1962 war dispute. India maintains it as legal border; China rejects.

nodes.label: Forward Policy (1961-62)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Indian military posture under Nehru-Menon — establishing forward posts in disputed Aksai Chin and NEFA to assert sovereignty without reinforcing logistics. Provoked Chinese response. Military unprepared. Led to disastrous 1962 war.

nodes.label: Aftermath of 1962 China War
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Nehru's prestige shattered; Krishna Menon resigned. Emergency (external) proclaimed 1962. India rapidly expanded army (from 0.5M to 1M) and air force (82 to 45 squadrons target). Parliamentary 'no resolution' that India would recover every inch. Emotional blow hastened Nehru's decline; died May 1964.

nodes.label: Nehru's Death (27 May 1964)
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Jawaharlal Nehru died 27 May 1964 at 74, of stroke preceded by heart attack Jan 1964. End of 17-year premiership. Kamaraj Plan (1963) had prepared but not resolved succession. Gulzarilal Nanda acting PM. Lal Bahadur Shastri elected by Syndicate as successor June 1964.

nodes.label: Gulzarilal Nanda (Acting PM)
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Home Minister who served as acting PM twice: after Nehru's death (27 May - 9 June 1964) and after Shastri's death (11-24 Jan 1966). Gandhian, Planning Commission member. Never a contender for full PM-ship.

nodes.label: Indira Gandhi Becomes PM (24 Jan 1966)
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: After Shastri's death at Tashkent (11 Jan 1966), Syndicate chose Indira as compromise against Morarji Desai. Parliamentary party vote 355-169. Seen as malleable 'gungi gudiya' (dumb doll). Proved otherwise by 1969 bank nationalisation and 1971 war.

nodes.label: Rupee Devaluation (June 1966)
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: 6 June 1966 — Indian rupee devalued 36.5% against USD (Rs 4.76 to Rs 7.50) under US/World Bank pressure for economic aid amid BOP crisis. Politically disastrous for Indira. Led to backlash against 'IMF dependence' and Congress election setback 1967.

nodes.label: 1967 General Elections
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Feb 1967 — Congress vote down to 40.8%, lost 8 states to opposition coalitions (SVDs). Ram Manohar Lohia's 'anti-Congressism' succeeded. Early collapse of Congress System. Birth of SVD (Samyukta Vidhayak Dal) coalition politics in states.

nodes.label: V.V. Giri (4th President, 1969-74)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Independent candidate (conscience vote) backed by Indira in 1969 presidential election against Syndicate's Sanjiva Reddy. Won by 17,366 votes. Former Labour Minister. His victory precipitated Congress split.

nodes.label: Abolition of Privy Purses (1971)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Indira's 1970 ordinance de-recognising princes failed in Supreme Court (Madhavrao Scindia case). 26th Constitutional Amendment Dec 1971 abolished privy purses and princely privileges permanently. Indira's populist move; ~Rs 4 crore/year savings but huge symbolic statement.

nodes.label: 26th Constitutional Amendment (1971)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Abolished privy purses and official recognition of former princely rulers. Omitted Articles 291 and 362, inserted Article 363A. Response to SC striking down 1970 ordinance. Ratified Dec 1971.

nodes.label: 24th Constitutional Amendment (1971)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Nov 1971 — Reasserted Parliament's power to amend any part of Constitution including Fundamental Rights. Response to Golaknath (1967). Amended Articles 13 and 368. Set stage for Kesavananda Bharati (1973).

nodes.label: 25th Constitutional Amendment (1971)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: April 1972 (passed 1971). Curtailed Right to Property (Article 31) to enable social welfare laws. Reduced compensation review. Added Article 31C giving primacy to DPSPs (Articles 39b, 39c) over FRs (14, 19, 31). Part of Indira's 1971 mandate bundle.

nodes.label: Garibi Hatao Slogan (1971)
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Indira's election slogan for 1971 mid-term polls. Promised poverty eradication. Won landslide 352/518 LS seats. Political success, economic results disputed — poverty ratio in 1973-74 was 55%, largely unchanged.

nodes.label: 1971 Lok Sabha Elections
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: March 1971 mid-term poll (after Congress split). Indira's Congress-R swept 352/518 seats with 43.7% vote. 'Indira hatao vs Garibi hatao' contest. Consolidated Indira's personal authority. 1971 Bangladesh War followed immediately after.

nodes.label: Basic Structure Doctrine (Kesavananda Bharati, 1973)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: SC ruling 24 April 1973 by 13-judge bench (7-6 majority). Established that Parliament can amend any part of Constitution but cannot alter its 'basic structure'. Chief Justice Sikri. Features: supremacy of Constitution, democratic republic, federalism, secularism, separation of powers, judicial review etc. Reaffirmed and expanded in Minerva Mills (1980).

nodes.label: Allahabad HC Judgment (12 June 1975)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Justice Jagmohanlal Sinha ruled in Raj Narain vs Indira Gandhi that Indira's 1971 Rae Bareli election was corrupt (misuse of govt machinery). Declared her election void, barred her from holding office for 6 years. Triggered Emergency declaration 13 days later (25 June 1975).

nodes.label: Raj Narain
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Socialist politician, losing candidate against Indira in 1971 Rae Bareli. His election petition led to Allahabad HC judgment June 1975. Defeated Indira in 1977 Rae Bareli. Later health minister in Janata govt. Eccentric, colourful figure.

nodes.label: Emergency Declaration (25 June 1975)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: President Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed proclaimed Emergency under Article 352 on grounds of internal disturbance, at Indira's advice midnight 25 June. No cabinet consultation (ex-post ratification). Based on JP Movement, Allahabad HC judgment. Lasted 21 months till 21 March 1977.

nodes.label: Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed (5th President)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: President 1974-77. Signed Emergency proclamation 25 June 1975 midnight on Indira's advice. Famous/infamous for rubber-stamping ordinances 'from his bathtub'. Died Feb 1977 in office.

nodes.label: Maintenance of Internal Security Act (MISA)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: 1971 act allowing preventive detention without trial. Amended during Emergency (1975) to increase detention periods and bar judicial review. Used to detain opposition leaders (JP Narayan, Morarji Desai, Advani, Vajpayee, 110,000+ total). Repealed 1978 by Janata govt.

nodes.label: ADM Jabalpur vs Shivkant Shukla (1976)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: SC's notorious 'Habeas Corpus Case' — 4-1 majority ruling that right to life and personal liberty (Art 21) could be suspended during Emergency. Justice H.R. Khanna's lone dissent (cost him CJI). Widely considered SC's darkest hour. Overruled by Puttaswamy (2017).

nodes.label: 42nd Amendment — 'Mini-Constitution' (1976)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Swaran Singh Committee proposals enacted Dec 1976. Added Part IV-A (Fundamental Duties), inserted 'Socialist', 'Secular', 'Integrity' in Preamble, extended LS/Assembly term 5→6 years, curtailed judicial review, made DPSPs override FRs, transferred education etc. to Concurrent List. Largest amendment ever. Mostly reversed by 44th (1978).

nodes.label: Sanjay Gandhi
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Indira's younger son (1946-1980). Emerged as extra-constitutional authority during Emergency. Led 5-Point Programme: family planning (forced sterilisations 8M+ done), tree planting, adult literacy, dowry ban, slum clearance (Turkman Gate demolitions). Died Jun 1980 plane crash.

nodes.label: Turkman Gate Demolitions (April 1976)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Forced slum-clearance in Old Delhi by Sanjay Gandhi's DDA. Bulldozers razed homes of poor (Muslim) residents. Police firing killed protesters. Symbol of Emergency excesses. Enduring political scar.

nodes.label: 1977 General Elections
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: March 1977 — first non-Congress govt at Centre. Janata Party swept 298/542 seats (41%). Congress crashed to 154 (34%). Indira and Sanjay lost their seats. JP Narayan's moral leadership + anti-Emergency backlash. Morarji Desai became PM at 81.

nodes.label: 44th Amendment (1978) — Reversal
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Janata govt's landmark reversal of 42nd Amendment. Removed Right to Property from FRs (made Article 300A legal right), restored judicial review, required written cabinet advice for Emergency, narrowed Article 352 to 'armed rebellion' (from 'internal disturbance'), required written cabinet note, restored Supreme Court/HC jurisdiction.

nodes.label: Janata Party Split (July 1979)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Charan Singh revolted over 'dual membership' (Jana Sangh members' RSS ties). Raj Narain expelled. Morarji resigned 15 July. Charan Singh sworn in 28 July with Indira's promised support — but she withdrew, forcing fresh polls Jan 1980.

nodes.label: 1980 General Elections
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Jan 1980 — Indira's Congress-I returned with 353/529 LS seats (42.7%). Janata collapsed. 'Indira is India' campaign. Sanjay Gandhi emerged stronger — but died Jun 1980 in plane crash. Rajiv reluctantly entered politics.

nodes.label: Mandal Commission (1979)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Second Backward Classes Commission chaired by B.P. Mandal. Appointed Dec 1978 by Morarji govt under Article 340. Submitted report Dec 1980 — recommended 27% reservation for OBCs (in addition to 22.5% SC/ST). Shelved till VP Singh implemented 1990.

nodes.label: B.P. Mandal
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Former Bihar CM, chairman of Second Backward Classes Commission (1979-80). Report recommended 27% OBC reservation. Name synonymous with OBC quota. Died 1982 — didn't live to see implementation.

nodes.label: Bhopal Gas Tragedy (3 Dec 1984)
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Union Carbide India Ltd pesticide plant leaked 40 tons methyl isocyanate (MIC). 3,787 immediate deaths; 15,000+ over time; 500,000+ affected. Warren Anderson (UCC CEO) briefly arrested, released on bail — never faced trial. Rs 715 crore settlement 1989. World's worst industrial disaster.

nodes.label: 1984 Anti-Sikh Riots (Nov 1984)
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: After Indira's assassination 31 Oct 1984, organised mob violence against Sikhs in Delhi (2,733 killed officially, 3,000+ per unofficial) and other cities. Congress leaders implicated. Rajiv's 'when a big tree falls...' remark. Enduring trauma. Commissions: Mishra (1985), Nanavati (2000).

nodes.label: Assam Accord (14-15 Aug 1985)
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Signed between Rajiv and All Assam Students' Union (AASU) / Assam Gana Sangram Parishad leaders. Set 25 March 1971 as cutoff for detection/deportation of illegal Bangladeshi immigrants. Promised protection of Assamese identity (Clause 6). Led to AGP formation 1985 and 1985 Assembly polls.

nodes.label: Mizo Accord (30 June 1986)
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Signed by Rajiv and Laldenga's Mizo National Front. Ended 20-year MNF insurgency. Created Mizoram statehood (1987) from UT. Laldenga became first CM. Model for peaceful insurgency resolution. Perhaps most successful accord.

nodes.label: Rajiv-Longowal Accord / Punjab Accord (24 July 1985)
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Rajiv and Sant Harchand Singh Longowal (Akali Dal moderate) signed accord addressing Anandpur Sahib demands partially. Transfer of Chandigarh to Punjab (never happened), Ravi-Beas waters tribunal, Army deserters treatment. Longowal assassinated 20 Aug 1985 by militants. Accord largely unimplemented.

nodes.label: Jarnail Singh Bhindranwale
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Radical Sikh preacher, leader of Damdami Taksal. Initially backed by Congress (Zail Singh, Sanjay) to undercut Akalis. Mobilised for Sikh separatism, sheltered militants. Took over Akal Takht in Golden Temple 1983. Killed in Operation Blue Star June 1984.

nodes.label: 52nd Amendment — Anti-Defection Law (1985)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Rajiv era. Inserted Tenth Schedule. Disqualifies MPs/MLAs for voluntarily giving up party membership, voting against party whip. Provided exemption for 'split' (1/3rd defection) — removed by 91st Amendment 2003. Major cleanup of 'aya ram gaya ram' politics.

nodes.label: Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Divorce) Act (1986)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Rajiv's Parliament overturned Shah Bano SC verdict (1985) under orthodox Muslim clerical pressure. Limited maintenance to iddat period (~3 months), devolved responsibility to Waqf Board. Major political misstep — perceived minority appeasement. Followed by Shilanyas at Ayodhya 1989 (counterbalance to Hindu votes).

nodes.label: Shilanyas at Ayodhya (Nov 1989)
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Nov 1989 — Rajiv govt allowed VHP to perform foundation-stone laying (shilanyas) of Ram Mandir at disputed Babri Masjid site (Ayodhya), to counterbalance Shah Bano reversal perception. Major concession to Hindu sentiment. Accelerated Ayodhya movement.

nodes.label: Bofors Scandal (1987 onwards)
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: April 1987 Swedish Radio revealed kickbacks in Rs 1,437 crore Bofors 155mm howitzer deal (1986). Rs 64 crore paid to Ottavio Quattrocchi (Rajiv's friend). V.P. Singh (FM, then Defence) resigned, broke away to form Jan Morcha (1988). Defined 1989 elections — Rajiv lost. Case dragged decades.

nodes.label: IPKF in Sri Lanka (1987-90)
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Indian Peace Keeping Force deployed under Rajiv-Jayewardene Accord (29 July 1987). Meant to disarm LTTE after Indo-Sri Lanka Peace Accord. Turned into war with LTTE (80,000 troops peak, 1,200+ Indian casualties). Withdrawn March 1990. Rajiv assassinated by LTTE 21 May 1991 in revenge.

nodes.label: LTTE (Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam)
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Sri Lankan Tamil militant separatist group founded 1976 by Velupillai Prabhakaran. Initially trained in India (Tamil Nadu camps, 1980s). Fought IPKF 1987-90. Pioneered suicide-vest bombing (assassinated Rajiv 1991, Premadasa 1993). Defeated by Sri Lankan army May 2009.

nodes.label: 1989 General Elections
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Nov 1989 — Congress reduced to 197/529 seats. National Front (VP Singh's Janata Dal + allies, 143 seats) formed minority govt with outside support from BJP (85) and Left (52). Bofors, Shah Bano, Ayodhya shaped vote.

nodes.label: C.N. Annadurai
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Founded DMK 1949 (split from Periyar's DK). TN CM 1967-69 after DMK historic 1967 victory. Ended decade of anti-Hindi agitation. Died Feb 1969 of cancer. Succeeded by Karunanidhi. Pioneer of Dravidian political cinema.

nodes.label: DMK (Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Founded 1949 by C.N. Annadurai splitting from Periyar's DK. Dravidian regional party. Won TN 1967 elections (ending Congress rule, never returned). Split 1972 creating AIADMK (MGR). Alternated TN govt with AIADMK ever since. Family dominance under Karunanidhi-Stalin.

nodes.label: M. Karunanidhi
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: TN CM five terms (1969-71, 1971-76, 1989-91, 1996-2001, 2006-11). Annadurai's successor. Tamil scholar-politician. Party split in 1972 creating AIADMK. Long DMK patriarch till 2018 death.

nodes.label: M.G. Ramachandran (MGR) & AIADMK (1972)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Matinee idol who broke from DMK 1972 to found AIADMK. TN CM 1977 till death 1987. Introduced midday meal scheme 1982 (national model). Charismatic mass leader. Succeeded by Jayalalithaa.

nodes.label: Anti-Hindi Agitation (1965)
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Jan-Feb 1965 TN agitation against Hindi becoming sole official language from 26 Jan 1965 (15-year transition per Article 343). Student riots, self-immolations (70+ deaths). Shastri govt passed Official Languages Act 1963 then amended 1967 — guaranteed English continuation. Catapulted DMK to 1967 power.

nodes.label: N.T. Rama Rao & TDP (1982)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Telugu film star founded Telugu Desam Party 29 March 1982. Won Andhra Pradesh 1983 (202/294 seats) — first non-Congress state govt in AP. 'Telugu pride' against Congress. Dismissed by Governor 1984 but reinstated after protests. 3x CM (1983-88, 1994-95). Model for regional ethno-linguistic mobilisation.

nodes.label: Left Front Government in West Bengal (1977-2011)
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: CPI(M)-led coalition won 1977 WB elections (231/294 seats). Jyoti Basu CM till 2000, then Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee till 2011. World's longest-running democratically-elected communist govt (34 years). Operation Barga land tenancy reform 1978. Eventually lost to Mamata's TMC 2011.

nodes.label: Jyoti Basu
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: CPI(M) stalwart, WB CM 1977-2000 (23 years, longest serving). Declined PM-ship in 1996 despite United Front offer (CPI(M) Politburo veto — 'historic blunder' he later called). Barrister-turned-trade-unionist. Died 2010.

nodes.label: Naxalbari Uprising (May 1967)
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: May 1967 peasant uprising in Naxalbari, Darjeeling district (WB). Led by CPI(M) cadres Charu Majumdar, Kanu Sanyal, Jangal Santhal. Landlord killed; police retaliation killed 11. Spark for Naxalite movement. Broke from CPI(M), formed CPI(ML) 1969. Spread to AP, Bihar; state crushed by 1972.

nodes.label: Farooq Abdullah
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Son of Sheikh Abdullah. J&K CM 1982-84, dismissed by Jagmohan. Rajiv-Farooq Accord 1986. CM 1986-90 (resigned when Jagmohan returned as Governor amid insurgency). Later CM 1996-2002. Union Minister under UPA.

nodes.label: Industrial Policy Resolution (1948)
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: First IPR. Classified industries into 4 groups: (1) Central monopoly — arms, atomic energy, railways; (2) New govt undertakings — coal, iron/steel, aircraft, shipping, telegraphs; (3) 18 industries state-regulated; (4) rest private. Mixed-economy framework. Replaced by IPR 1956.

nodes.label: Feldman-Mahalanobis Model
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Economic development model emphasising heavy capital-goods industries to achieve self-reliance and growth. Borrowed from Soviet economist G.A. Feldman (1928); adapted by P.C. Mahalanobis for India's Second Plan (1956-61). Theoretical basis for public-sector heavy industry.

nodes.label: Bhakra Nangal Dam
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Multipurpose project on Sutlej (Punjab-Himachal). Conceived pre-1947, construction 1948-63 under First & Second Plans. Dedicated by Nehru 22 Oct 1963 as 'new temple of resurgent India'. Then India's highest dam (226m). Symbol of Nehruvian vision.

nodes.label: Hirakud Dam
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: On Mahanadi (Odisha). First major post-independence dam, started 1948, inaugurated by Nehru 13 Jan 1957. Then world's longest dam (26km). Flood control + irrigation + hydropower.

nodes.label: Damodar Valley Corporation (1948)
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Set up July 1948 — first river valley authority modelled on TVA (Tennessee Valley). Covers Damodar basin (Jharkhand-WB). Multipurpose: flood control, irrigation, power, navigation. Flagship Nehruvian public-sector institution.

nodes.label: Bhilai-Rourkela-Durgapur Steel Plants
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Three public-sector steel mills under Second Plan: Bhilai (1955, Soviet help), Rourkela (1955, West German), Durgapur (1956, UK). Plus expansion of Tata Iron & Steel, Hindustan Steel. Core of industrial self-reliance strategy.

nodes.label: MRTP Act (1969)
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices Act 1969. Based on Mahalanobis Committee 1964 + Dutt Committee 1969 findings that Tatas/Birlas concentrated too much economic power. Required MRTP Commission approval for expansion/merger by big houses. Repealed/replaced by Competition Act 2002.

nodes.label: FERA (Foreign Exchange Regulation Act, 1973)
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Indira era. Tight restrictions on foreign companies — forex controls required dilution to 40% foreign equity. IBM and Coca-Cola exited India 1977 rather than dilute. Replaced by FEMA 1999.

nodes.label: Nationalisation of Coal (1971-73)
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Coking Coal Mines Nationalisation Act 1971 + Coal Mines Nationalisation Act 1973. Coal India Limited established 1975. Indira era — extension of public-sector dominance. Preceded by 1969 bank nationalisation.

nodes.label: Nationalisation of General Insurance (1972)
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: General Insurance Business (Nationalisation) Act 1972 — 107 insurers nationalised into 4 subsidiaries of GIC (General Insurance Corp). Followed LIC nationalisation (1956). Reversed by 1999 IRDA Act.

nodes.label: 1966 Rupee Devaluation
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: See hist_rupee_devaluation_1966. Economics angle: broke fixed-exchange-rate peg, 36.5% devaluation. Prompted by Third Plan failures, 1965 war, drought, US aid conditionality (PL-480 'ship-to-mouth'). Failed to boost exports quickly; politically toxic.

nodes.label: Five Year Plan Growth Rates (1951-1990)
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: 1st (3.6%), 2nd (4.0-4.3%), 3rd (2.8% failed), 4th (3.3%), 5th (4.8%), 6th (5.7% first to beat target), 7th (6%). Average ~3.5% 'Hindu rate of growth' through 1950-80s. Accelerated post-1980 with deregulation.

nodes.label: Hindu Rate of Growth
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Term coined by Raj Krishna (1978) for India's 3.5% annual growth 1950-80, low vs East Asia's 7-10%. Derogatory — implied stagnation due to planning-era constraints. Broken by 1980s partial liberalisation (5.5%) and decisively by 1991 reforms.

nodes.label: Zamindari Abolition (1950s)
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Multiple state laws 1947-56 abolishing zamindari, jagirdari, inamdari. UP Zamindari Abolition Act 1950; Bihar 1950; West Bengal Estates Acquisition 1953. Transferred land from 'intermediaries' to actual tillers (ryots). First-phase land reform — largely successful.

nodes.label: Bhoodan Movement
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Vinoba Bhave's land-gift movement from 1951 (started Pochampalli, AP). Persuaded landlords to donate land to landless. ~4.4M acres gifted by 1960s; ~2.5M actually distributed. Extended to Gramdan (village-collective ownership). Peaceful alternative to radical land redistribution. Substantially wound down by 1970.

nodes.label: Vinoba Bhave
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Gandhian disciple (1895-1982). Led Bhoodan (1951) and Gramdan movements. First Bharat Ratna recipient 1983 (posthumous). 'Acharya' status. Also supported Emergency ('anushasan parv' — time of discipline).

nodes.label: Cooperative Movement in India
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Post-1947 expansion — AMUL (1946), cooperative credit societies, IFFCO (1967), KRIBHCO (1980). Nagpur Resolution 1959 pushed 'cooperative joint farming' (failed). Kerala/WB strong. Cooperative federalism through Vaidyanathan Committee.

nodes.label: HYV (High-Yielding Variety) Seeds
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Dwarf wheat varieties imported from Mexico (Norman Borlaug, CIMMYT) and rice from IRRI Philippines. Mexican wheat: Sonora-64, Lerma Rojo. Adopted 1966 onwards. Wheat yield doubled. Required complementary inputs (fertiliser, irrigation, credit, MSP).

nodes.label: Food Corporation of India (1965)
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Established 1965 under Food Corporations Act. Procures food grains at MSP, maintains buffer stock, distributes through PDS. Core of India's food security system. C. Subramaniam's creation.

nodes.label: Agricultural Prices Commission (APC, 1965)
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Set up Jan 1965 to recommend MSP for crops. Renamed CACP (Commission for Agricultural Costs & Prices) 1985. Key institution enabling Green Revolution by assuring farmers remunerative prices.

nodes.label: Minimum Support Price (MSP)
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Govt-guaranteed procurement floor price for key crops. Started 1966-67 for wheat, extended to 23+ crops. Recommended by APC/CACP. Backbone of Green Revolution incentive structure. Major farmer protest issue late 2010s onwards.

nodes.label: 1969 Ahmedabad Riots
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: 18-28 Sept 1969 Hindu-Muslim riots, ~500-2,000 deaths (disputed). First major post-independence communal violence. Trigger: cow-dispute. Reddy Commission found systematic. Set template for subsequent riots. Gandhi's birthplace irony.

nodes.label: Bhiwandi Riots (May 1970)
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Bhiwandi-Jalgaon-Mahad riots in Maharashtra May 1970. 200+ killed, mostly Muslim. Sparked by Shivaji Jayanti procession. Madon Commission. Indira govt called out army. Pattern of planned communal violence tied to politics.

nodes.label: Ram Janmabhoomi Movement (1980s)
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: VHP-led campaign from early 1980s to 'liberate' Babri Masjid site (claimed as Ram's birthplace). Shilanyas 1989, LK Advani's Rath Yatra Sept-Oct 1990. VP Singh govt fell blocking yatra. Mosque demolished 6 Dec 1992 (era-11 boundary).

nodes.label: Advani's Rath Yatra (Sept-Oct 1990)
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: L.K. Advani's BJP Rath Yatra from Somnath to Ayodhya in 'Toyota chariot' — Ram temple campaign. 10,000km through 8 states. Arrested in Bihar by Lalu Yadav 23 Oct 1990. BJP withdrew support from VP Singh govt, which fell 7 Nov 1990.

nodes.label: Mandal Commission Implementation (Aug 1990)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: VP Singh govt implemented 27% OBC reservation on 7 Aug 1990 (Mandal Report's 10-year-old recommendation). Massive anti-reservation protests by upper caste students — 159 self-immolations, Rajiv Goswami Sept 1990 first and iconic. Supreme Court upheld reservation in Indra Sawhney (1992) but capped total at 50%.

nodes.label: Indra Sawhney Case (1992)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: 9-judge SC bench Nov 1992. Upheld 27% OBC reservation (Mandal). Introduced: 'creamy layer' exclusion, 50% overall reservation cap, reservations only in initial appointment (not promotions — later amended by 77th Amendment 1995).

nodes.label: Towards Equality Report (1974)
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: First govt report on status of women in India (Dec 1974). Committee chaired by Phulrenu Guha under Education Ministry. Documented widening gender gaps post-1947 — declining sex ratio, limited gains from law. Catalyst for feminist movement of late 1970s.

nodes.label: Mathura Rape Case (1972/1979)
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: 14-year-old tribal girl raped 1972 in Desaiganj police station, Maharashtra. SC 1979 acquitted officers — 'no injuries' → 'consent'. Public outrage. Open letter by 4 law professors. Led to Criminal Law (Second Amendment) Act 1983 — burden-of-proof shift in custodial rape cases.

nodes.label: Chipko Movement (1973)
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Tree-hugging environmental movement in Garhwal (Uttarakhand). Led by Chandi Prasad Bhatt, Sunderlal Bahuguna, Gaura Devi. 1973 Reni village women hugged trees to prevent felling. Spawned decentralised forest policy. Inspired global eco-movement. Forest Conservation Act 1980 partially a response.

nodes.label: Narmada Bachao Andolan (1985 onwards)
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Led by Medha Patkar from 1985 against Sardar Sarovar Dam (Narmada). Raised rehabilitation, environmental costs. World Bank withdrew 1993 after Morse Review. SC in Narmada case (2000) allowed dam at reduced height. Landmark environmental-justice movement.

nodes.label: Silent Valley Movement (Kerala, 1970s-80s)
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Campaign against Silent Valley hydel project in Kerala's Western Ghats. KSSP (Kerala Sasthra Sahitya Parishat) led. Indira Gandhi scrapped project Jan 1981. Silent Valley declared national park 1984. Early environmental victory.

nodes.label: Progressive Artists' Group (Bombay, 1947)
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Founded Aug 1947 Bombay by F.N. Souza, K.H. Ara, S.H. Raza, M.F. Husain, S.K. Bakre, H.A. Gade. Broke from Bengal School, embraced modernism (Cubism, Expressionism). Disbanded 1956, but members became giants of Indian modern art.

nodes.label: Pather Panchali (1955) / Parallel Cinema
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Satyajit Ray's debut, Apu Trilogy first film (1955). Launched Indian parallel/art cinema. Won best human document at Cannes 1956. Other masters: Ritwik Ghatak, Mrinal Sen, Bimal Roy. Later 1970s: Shyam Benegal, Govind Nihalani.

nodes.label: Sahitya Akademi (1954)
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: National Academy of Letters. Inaugurated 12 March 1954 in Delhi. Promotes Indian literature in 24 recognised languages. Sahitya Akademi Awards annually since 1955. Autonomous under Culture Ministry.

nodes.label: Sangeet Natak Akademi (1952)
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: India's first national academy for performing arts (music, dance, drama). Founded Jan 1953 (registered 1952). Autonomous body under Culture Ministry. SNA Awards, Ratna Sadasya. Based in Delhi.

nodes.label: Lalit Kala Akademi (1954)
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: National Academy of Fine Arts. Founded 5 Aug 1954. Promotes Indian fine arts, organises Triennale India, supports artists. Rashtriya Lalit Kala Ratna awards. Part of trio with Sahitya and Sangeet Natak Akademis.

nodes.label: 4th Amendment (1955)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Put compensation scale for compulsory land acquisition beyond court scrutiny. Authorised state to nationalise any trade. Added more Acts to Ninth Schedule. Extended scope of Article 31A. Response to Bela Banerjee case.

nodes.label: 9th Amendment (1960) — Berubari
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Facilitated cession of Berubari Union (West Bengal) to Pakistan per Indo-Pakistan Agreement 1958 (Nehru-Noon). Passed after SC's Berubari Union case (1960) held that territorial cession requires constitutional amendment. Never actually notified for implementation.

nodes.label: 12th Amendment (1962) — Goa, Daman, Diu
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Incorporated Goa, Daman and Diu into Indian Union after Dec 1961 liberation. Added to Union Territory list.

nodes.label: 13th Amendment (1962) — Nagaland Statehood
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Granted statehood to Nagaland (carved from Assam) with special provisions under Article 371A. Response to Naga insurgency and 1960 Naga agreement. Nagaland became 16th state on 1 Dec 1963.

nodes.label: 14th Amendment (1962) — Puducherry
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Incorporated Puducherry (then Pondicherry) into Indian Union following 1954 merger. Created legislatures for Himachal Pradesh, Manipur, Tripura, Goa Daman Diu, Puducherry (all then UTs).

nodes.label: 16th Amendment (1963) — Sovereignty Restrictions
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Empowered state to restrict freedom of speech/assembly/association in interests of sovereignty and integrity of India. Added 'integrity' to oath. Response to DMK's earlier separatist rhetoric in Tamil Nadu.

nodes.label: 17th Amendment (1964) — Ninth Schedule Expansion
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Required market-value compensation for land under personal cultivation. Added 44 more Acts to Ninth Schedule. Response to Karimbil Kunhikoman case (Kerala).

nodes.label: 21st Amendment (1967) — Sindhi Added
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Added Sindhi as 15th language in Eighth Schedule. Response to Sindhi-speaking community's demand after Partition displacement.

nodes.label: 22nd Amendment (1969) — Meghalaya
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Created autonomous state of Meghalaya within Assam (Khasi, Jaintia, Garo Hills). Meghalaya became full state via 23rd Constitutional (Amendment) Act 1972 + NE Reorganisation Act 1971.

nodes.label: 31st Amendment (1972) — Lok Sabha 525→545
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Increased Lok Sabha strength from 525 to 545 seats. Froze state-wise LS seat distribution based on 1971 census (further frozen 2001 till 2026 by 84th Amendment).

nodes.label: 36th Amendment (1975) — Sikkim Statehood
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Made Sikkim 22nd full state of Indian Union on 26 April 1975, replacing 'associate state' status under 35th Amendment 1974. Chogyal monarchy abolished after 1975 referendum (97.5% for merger).

nodes.label: 38th Amendment (1975) — Emergency Non-Justiciable
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Emergency-era amendment. Made President's proclamation of Emergency and ordinances non-justiciable. Empowered President to declare Emergency on different grounds simultaneously. Reversed by 44th Amendment 1978.

nodes.label: 39th Amendment (1975) — Election Protection
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Indira's shield after Allahabad HC verdict (June 1975). Placed elections of PM, President, VP, Speaker beyond judicial review. Struck down in Indira Nehru Gandhi vs Raj Narain (1975) — SC invoked basic structure doctrine for first time.

nodes.label: 40th Amendment (1976) — Maritime Zones
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Empowered Parliament to specify territorial waters, EEZ (Exclusive Economic Zone), continental shelf, maritime zones of India. Constitutional basis for Maritime Zones Act 1976.

nodes.label: 58th Amendment (1987) — Hindi Constitution
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Provided authoritative text of Constitution in Hindi language, giving same legal sanctity as English version. Article 394A added.

nodes.label: 61st Amendment (1989) — Voting Age 18
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Reduced voting age from 21 to 18 years for LS and Assembly elections. Article 326 amended. Rajiv Gandhi's initiative. Added ~5 crore young voters. Took effect before 1989 general elections.

nodes.label: 65th Amendment (1990) — NC for SC/ST
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Established multi-member National Commission for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Article 338), replacing single Special Officer. Later split into two separate commissions by 89th Amendment 2003.

nodes.label: Constitutional Amendments 1950-1990 (Overview)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: 65 amendments passed 1951-1990, 4 themes: (1) State reorganisation — 7th, 9th, 12th-14th, 18th, 22nd, 27th, 35th, 36th, 53rd-57th; (2) SC/ST/OBC reservation extensions — 8th, 23rd, 45th, 51st, 62nd; (3) Land reform / 9th Schedule — 1st, 4th, 17th, 29th, 34th, 40th, 47th, 66th; (4) Emergency + judicial — 24-26th, 38th-42nd (authoritarian), 43rd-44th (restoration).

nodes.label: A.K. Gopalan Case (1950)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: A.K. Gopalan vs State of Madras, first major post-constitution SC case. Challenged Preventive Detention Act 1950. SC held narrow interpretation — Articles 19, 21, 22 were mutually exclusive. Procedure 'established by law' literal (not due process). Overruled by Maneka Gandhi (1978).

nodes.label: Champakam Dorairajan Case (1951)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: State of Madras vs Champakam Dorairajan. Madras Communal GO providing caste-based reservation struck down. Led to 1st Constitutional Amendment 1951 adding Article 15(4) authorising special provisions for socially/educationally backward classes.

nodes.label: Romesh Thappar Case (1950)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Romesh Thappar vs State of Madras 1950. Communist magazine 'Cross Roads' banned. SC struck down Madras Maintenance of Public Order Act. Expanded free speech under Article 19(1)(a). Led to 1st Amendment 1951 adding 'public order' as permissible restriction.

nodes.label: Shankari Prasad Case (1951)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Shankari Prasad Singh Deo vs Union of India 1951. Challenge to 1st Amendment. SC held Parliament can amend Fundamental Rights under Article 368; 'law' in Article 13(2) means ordinary law, not constitutional amendment. Reaffirmed in Sajjan Singh (1965), reversed by Golaknath (1967).

nodes.label: Sajjan Singh Case (1965)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Sajjan Singh vs State of Rajasthan 1965. Challenge to 17th Amendment. SC (5-judge) 3-2 reaffirmed Shankari Prasad — Parliament can amend FRs. But minority (Hidayatullah, Mudholkar) expressed doubts — seed of Golaknath.

nodes.label: Berubari Union Case (1960)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: In Re: Berubari Union 1960. Presidential Reference on Nehru-Noon agreement's cession of Berubari to Pakistan. SC held territorial cession requires constitutional amendment (not just ordinary law). Also held Preamble is not part of Constitution (later reversed in Kesavananda 1973). Led to 9th Amendment 1960.

nodes.label: Indira Nehru Gandhi vs Raj Narain (1975)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: SC 7 Nov 1975 struck down 39th Amendment (1975) which placed PM's election beyond judicial review. First application of basic structure doctrine post-Kesavananda. Upheld Indira's election on merits via election law changes but doctrine stood. Judges: Ray CJ, Khanna, Mathew, Beg, Chandrachud Y.V.

nodes.label: Waman Rao Case (1981)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: SC 1981 held amendments to Ninth Schedule BEFORE 24 April 1973 (Kesavananda date) are valid; amendments AFTER that date are subject to basic structure review. 'Doctrine of prospective overruling'. Key case fencing basic structure doctrine.

nodes.label: Election Commission of India (25 Jan 1950)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Established 25 January 1950 under Article 324, one day before Constitution came into force. Single-member body (CEC) till 16 Oct 1989, then multi-member (CEC + 2 ECs) after 1991 (some flip-flops). First CEC: Sukumar Sen 1950-58. Key institution of Indian democracy.

nodes.label: Comptroller & Auditor General (CAG, 1950)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Constitutional body under Article 148. First CAG: V. Narahari Rao (1948-54). Audits Central and State govt accounts. 'Guardian of the public purse'. Submits report to President/Governor, tabled in Parliament/Assembly.

nodes.label: Union Public Service Commission (UPSC, 1950)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Constitutional body under Article 315. Conducts Civil Services, Engineering Services, other All-India exams. Successor to Federal Public Service Commission (1935). First Chairman post-1950: H.K. Kripalani.

nodes.label: Finance Commission (1951)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Constituted every 5 years under Article 280. Recommends Centre-State tax sharing, grants-in-aid. First FC: K.C. Neogy, 1951. K. Santhanam (FC-2), A.K. Chanda (FC-3), P.V. Rajamannar (FC-4), Mahavir Tyagi (FC-5), K. Brahmananda Reddy (FC-6), J.M. Shelat (FC-7), Y.B. Chavan (FC-8), N.K.P. Salve (FC-9).

nodes.label: Planning Commission (March 1950)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Established 15 March 1950 by Cabinet resolution (extra-constitutional). Nehru chaired ex-officio. Designed Five Year Plans. G.L. Nanda, C.M. Trivedi, P.C. Mahalanobis key architects. Replaced by NITI Aayog on 1 Jan 2015.

nodes.label: National Commission for Women (1990)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Statutory body under NCW Act 1990, constituted 31 Jan 1992. Recommends legal safeguards, investigates violations of women's rights. First chair: Jayanti Patnaik. Not a constitutional body (that's NCSC/ST).

nodes.label: External Emergency (1962-68)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: First national emergency under Article 352. Proclaimed 26 Oct 1962 during China war on grounds of 'external aggression'. Revoked 10 Jan 1968. Enabled DIR (Defence of India Rules), suspension of FRs.

nodes.label: External Emergency (1971-77)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Second national emergency, 3 Dec 1971 during Bangladesh War. Continued until March 1977. Overlapped with internal Emergency (1975-77). Never properly revoked before internal emergency. Janata govt revoked both.

nodes.label: First President's Rule — Kerala (1959)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: 31 July 1959 — Nehru dismissed first democratically elected communist state govt (E.M.S. Namboodiripad, CPI, Kerala 1957-59) under Article 356. Trigger: 'Liberation Struggle' against Education Bill. Controversial precedent for political abuse of Article 356. Used 100+ times since.

nodes.label: Ninth Schedule
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Added by 1st Amendment 1951 to protect land reform laws from judicial review. 284 acts added by 2018. I.R. Coelho case (2007) held that post-24 April 1973 additions are subject to basic structure review. Original purpose: save zamindari abolition laws.

nodes.label: Tenth Schedule — Anti-Defection
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Added by 52nd Amendment 1985. Provides grounds for disqualification of MPs/MLAs on defection. Originally had 'split' exemption (1/3rd), removed by 91st Amendment 2003 (only 'merger' with 2/3rd now). Speaker/Chairman decides disqualification (judicial review allowed after Kihoto Hollohan 1992).

nodes.label: Fundamental Duties (Part IV-A, 1976)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Added by 42nd Amendment 1976 on Swaran Singh Committee recommendation (inspired by USSR Constitution). Originally 10 duties; 11th added by 86th Amendment 2002 (parental duty to educate children 6-14). Non-justiciable, moral obligations.

nodes.label: Preamble Changes by 42nd Amendment (1976)
nodes.subject: polity
