nodes.detail: Added three words to Preamble: 'Socialist', 'Secular', 'Integrity' (last joined 'Unity and Integrity'). Changed 'Sovereign Democratic Republic' to 'Sovereign Socialist Secular Democratic Republic'. Preamble remains part of basic structure post-Kesavananda.

nodes.label: Swaran Singh Committee (1976)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Congress-appointed 12-member committee under Sardar Swaran Singh. Recommended Fundamental Duties, Preamble changes, DPSP/FR ordering, curtailing judicial review. Report used to enact 42nd Amendment 1976. Not a constitutional commission.

nodes.label: Official Languages Act (1963) + 1967 Amendment
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Parliament enacted 1963 to continue English as official language alongside Hindi indefinitely (not limited to 1965 deadline of Article 343). Amended 1967 after anti-Hindi agitations — guaranteed English continuation in non-Hindi states. Basis of current language policy.

nodes.label: Citizenship Act (1955)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Defines acquisition of Indian citizenship: birth, descent, registration, naturalisation, incorporation of territory. Articles 5-11 of Constitution left details to Parliament. Amended multiple times — 1985 (Assam), 1986, 1992, 2003, 2005, 2015, 2019 (CAA).

nodes.label: Preventive Detention Act (1950)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Enacted Feb 1950 under Article 22 — detention without trial. Challenged in A.K. Gopalan. Lapsed 1969. Succeeded by MISA (1971), National Security Act (1980), POTA (2002, repealed 2004), UAPA (amended). Critical era-10 civil liberties backdrop.

nodes.label: National Security Act (1980)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Preventive detention act passed by Indira govt 1980 to replace MISA (repealed 1978). Allows detention up to 12 months without trial on grounds of 'national security', 'public order'. Still in force. Used by Centre and states.

nodes.label: Official Secrets Act (1923)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Colonial-era espionage law retained by independent India. Makes disclosure of 'secret' official information a crime (2-14 years). Widely critiqued post-RTI (2005). Covered Bofors, ISRO spy case (1994) etc. Reform recommended by 2nd ARC 2006.

nodes.label: All India Services (IAS, IPS, IFoS)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Article 312 — services common to Centre and states. Originally IAS (successor to ICS, 1947) and IPS (from IP). Indian Forest Service added 1966. All AIS officers recruited by UPSC, state-cadre allocated, serve under both Centre/state. Sardar Patel's 'steel frame'.

nodes.label: ICS → IAS Transition (1947-50)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Indian Civil Service (ICS, 1858) continued briefly post-1947. Recast as IAS per Article 312 + 1951 All India Services Act. Patel as Home Minister defended 'steel frame' against opposition from princes and politicians. Pathway for ICS officers + new recruits.

nodes.label: Mahalanobis Plan (Second Plan)
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: P.C. Mahalanobis's heavy-industry growth model for Second Plan (1956-61). Four-sector model: investment goods, consumer manufactured goods, consumer household goods, services. Emphasis on capital-goods sector investment to build industrial base. Critics: Vakil, Brahmananda favoured wage-goods first.

nodes.label: LIC Nationalisation (1956)
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Life Insurance Corporation Act 1956 nationalised 245 private life-insurance companies into LIC on 1 Sept 1956. First major nationalisation of private financial sector. Response to several scandals in private insurance. LIC monopoly till 1999 IRDA Act.

nodes.label: State Bank of India (1955)
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: SBI Act 1955 nationalised Imperial Bank of India (originally 1921 amalgamation of 3 presidency banks — Bengal 1806, Bombay 1840, Madras 1843) into State Bank of India on 1 July 1955. First major bank nationalisation, 14 years before 1969.

nodes.label: Second Bank Nationalisation (1980)
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Six more private banks nationalised by Indira Gandhi on 15 April 1980: Andhra Bank, Corporation Bank, New Bank of India, Oriental Bank of Commerce, Punjab & Sind Bank, Vijaya Bank. Total 20 nationalised banks (1969 + 1980), covering 91% of deposits. Consolidation underway since 2019.

nodes.label: Reserve Bank of India (1935/1949)
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Established 1 April 1935 under RBI Act 1934 (era-9 boundary). Nationalised 1 Jan 1949 under RBI (Transfer to Public Ownership) Act 1948. Central bank — monetary policy, currency issue, banker to govt, regulator of banks. Key post-1947 institution.

nodes.label: NABARD (1982) & SIDBI (1990)
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: NABARD: National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development, 12 July 1982, on Shivaraman Committee recommendation. Apex rural-development bank. SIDBI: Small Industries Development Bank of India, 2 April 1990, apex for small-scale industry.

nodes.label: IDBI (1964)
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Industrial Development Bank of India, established 1 July 1964 as RBI subsidiary. Apex development financial institution (DFI) for industry. Became independent of RBI 1976. Converted to commercial bank 2004 (IDBI Bank). Archetype of DFI era.

nodes.label: IFCI (1948)
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Industrial Finance Corporation of India, 1948 (first DFI). Long-term finance for industry. Became public limited company 1993. Core of Nehruvian financial architecture — direct lending to Plan priorities.

nodes.label: ICICI (1955)
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation of India, 1955. Private-sector-oriented DFI, backed by World Bank, US, British firms, Indian private sector. Became ICICI Bank (first major reverse-merger 2002 — DFI merged into its subsidiary bank).

nodes.label: Maharashtra Employment Guarantee Scheme (1972)
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Maharashtra's 1972-77 drought relief EGS — guaranteed manual work within 5km, minimum wage. Pioneered wage-employment-as-right concept. Model for NREGA 2005 (era 11). Designed by V.S. Page, implemented by Vasantrao Naik govt.

nodes.label: Public Distribution System (PDS) — Expansion
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Originated WW2 rationing (Bengal 1943 famine). Expanded post-1965 with FCI procurement + ration shops. Universal till 1997 (TPDS with APL/BPL), 2013 NFSA moved to rights-based approach (era 11). India's largest food safety net.

nodes.label: Integrated Rural Development Programme (IRDP, 1978)
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Launched 1978-79 by Janata, expanded nationwide 1980. Self-employment + assets scheme for rural BPL households — subsidised credit for income-generating assets. Running for 20+ years; merged into SGSY (1999).

nodes.label: NREP (1980) + RLEGP (1983)
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Wage-employment schemes: National Rural Employment Programme (1980) + Rural Landless Employment Guarantee Programme (1983). Merged 1989 into Jawahar Rozgar Yojana (JRY). Manual-labour public works. Predecessor to NREGA (2005).

nodes.label: Jawahar Rozgar Yojana (1989)
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Launched 1 April 1989 by Rajiv Gandhi, merging NREP + RLEGP. Rural wage-employment with 30% for women, 30% for SC/ST. Local Panchayat implementation. Renamed JGSY 1999, absorbed into NREGA 2005.

nodes.label: Regional Rural Banks (RRBs, 1975)
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Established 2 Oct 1975 on Narasimham Committee (1975) recommendation. Joint ownership: Centre 50%, Sponsor Bank 35%, State 15%. Rural credit to small farmers, artisans, labourers. 196 RRBs at peak, consolidated to 43 by 2020.

nodes.label: BOP Crisis Build-up (1985-91)
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Rajiv-era fiscal deficit (8%+ of GDP), oil imports, short-term debt accumulation. 1990-91 Gulf War spiked oil. Forex reserves down to 15 days' imports by June 1991. Credit rating downgrades. IMF bailout contingent on liberalisation. Triggered 1991 reforms (era 11 opening).

nodes.label: Dutt Committee on Industrial Licensing (1969)
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Subimal Dutt Committee. Found that 20 large business houses cornered 2/3 of industrial licences 1956-66. Catalyst for MRTP Act 1969. Exposed licence-permit-quota raj's capture by established players.

nodes.label: Hazari Committee (1967)
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: R.K. Hazari Committee. Studied industrial planning and licensing. Found large business houses exploiting licensing system. Led to Monopolies Inquiry Commission (Mahalanobis Committee) 1964 follow-up, eventually MRTP 1969.

nodes.label: M.F. Husain
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Modernist painter (1915-2011), 'Picasso of India'. Member Progressive Artists' Group 1947. Horses, goddesses, Bharat Mata themes. Took Qatari citizenship 2010 amid Hindu-right controversies over nudes. Padma Shri 1966, Bhushan 1973, Vibhushan 1991.

nodes.label: S.H. Raza
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Modernist painter (1922-2016). Progressive Artists' Group founder. Lived in France 1950-2010. 'Bindu' series iconic. Padma Shri 1981, Padma Bhushan 2007, Padma Vibhushan 2013.

nodes.label: Ritwik Ghatak
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Bengali filmmaker (1925-1976). Along with Satyajit Ray and Mrinal Sen, defined Indian parallel cinema. Films: Meghe Dhaka Tara (1960), Subarnarekha (1965), Titash Ekti Nadir Naam (1973). Partition-obsessed themes.

nodes.label: Mrinal Sen
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Bengali filmmaker (1923-2018). Bhuvan Shome (1969) kickstarted parallel cinema movement with FFC (Film Finance Corp) funding. Calcutta trilogy (1971-73). Padma Bhushan, Dadasaheb Phalke 2003.

nodes.label: Shyam Benegal
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Parallel cinema director from 1970s. Ankur (1974), Nishant (1975), Manthan (1976, Operation Flood film crowdfunded by dairy farmers), Bhumika (1977). Discovered Shabana Azmi, Smita Patil, Naseeruddin Shah.

nodes.label: NCPA (1969)
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: National Centre for the Performing Arts, Mumbai. Founded 1969 by JRD Tata and Jamshed Bhabha. Premier performing arts venue — opera, Indian classical, theatre. Private initiative rare for culture.

nodes.label: ICCR (1950)
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Indian Council for Cultural Relations, founded 1950 by Maulana Azad (first Education Minister). External cultural diplomacy — exchange programmes, cultural centres abroad (Ichinichi 37+), scholarships for foreign students.

nodes.label: Sports Authority of India (1984)
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Established 1984 post-1982 Asian Games (Delhi). Apex sports body. Manages national training centres, talent identification. Under Youth Affairs and Sports Ministry.

nodes.label: 1982 Asian Games (Delhi)
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: 9th Asian Games, Delhi 19 Nov - 4 Dec 1982. India hosted after 1951. Built Nehru Stadium (Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium), new infrastructure. Colour TV launched nationwide for coverage — Doordarshan's first colour broadcast. 'Appu' elephant mascot. Political showcase for Indira.

nodes.label: Cricket World Cup 1983
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: India won 3rd Prudential Cricket World Cup on 25 June 1983 at Lord's, beating West Indies by 43 runs. Kapil Dev captain. Defining sporting moment — launched Indian cricket as mass phenomenon, laid ground for BCCI economic rise.

nodes.label: Doordarshan (1959)
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Launched 15 Sept 1959 as experimental TV service from Delhi. UNESCO assistance. Regular service 1965. Colour broadcasting from 1982 (Asian Games). National channel 1984. Monopoly till 1991 satellite TV.

nodes.label: All India Radio (AIR)
nodes.subject: history
nodes.detail: Successor to Indian State Broadcasting Service (1930). Named 'All India Radio' 1936; 'Akashvani' 1957. Vividh Bharati 1957 (popular music/entertainment). FM services from 1977. Originally under Ministry of I&B, autonomous Prasar Bharati since 1997.

nodes.label: Objectives Resolution (13 Dec 1946)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Moved by Nehru 13 Dec 1946, adopted 22 Jan 1947. Declared India as independent sovereign republic with justice-liberty-equality-fraternity. Became basis for Preamble. 8 clauses covering sovereign character, federal unit structure, guaranteed fundamental rights, minorities/backward classes/tribal areas protection, territorial integrity, world peace.

nodes.label: Article 1 — Name and Territory
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: 'India, that is Bharat, shall be a Union of States.' Asserts indestructible Union (vs destructible states). Berubari case (1960) held cession requires constitutional amendment. Territory = states + UTs + acquired territories. 'Union' preferred over 'Federation'.

nodes.label: S. Radhakrishnan (2nd President, 1962-67)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Philosopher-statesman. First VP 1952-62 under Rajendra Prasad. 2nd President 13 May 1962 - 13 May 1967. Birthday 5 Sept celebrated as Teachers' Day. Oxford Spalding Professor. Author of 'The Hindu View of Life'.

nodes.label: Zakir Husain (3rd President, 1967-69)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: First Muslim President of India, 13 May 1967 - died in office 3 May 1969. Educationist, founded Jamia Millia Islamia. Gandhian. First Indian President to die in office. Succeeded by V.V. Giri (as acting, then elected).

nodes.label: Neelam Sanjiva Reddy (6th President, 1977-82)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Only President elected unopposed (21 July 1977). Earlier defeated by V.V. Giri in 1969 (Congress Syndicate's candidate). Previous Speaker of LS, Andhra CM. Janata-backed. Presided over Janata collapse and Indira's 1980 return.

nodes.label: Giani Zail Singh (7th President, 1982-87)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: First Sikh President. 25 July 1982 - 25 July 1987. Punjab CM 1972-77. Home Minister 1980-82. Controversially signed Operation Blue Star order despite reservations. Used pocket veto on Postal Bill 1986. Swore in Rajiv Gandhi hours after Indira's assassination.

nodes.label: R. Venkataraman (8th President, 1987-92)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: 25 July 1987 - 25 July 1992. Presided over four PMs (Rajiv, VP Singh, Chandra Shekhar, Narasimha Rao) — political instability era. Appointed Chandra Shekhar PM Nov 1990. Authored 'My Presidential Years'.

nodes.label: Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI, 1963)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Established 1 April 1963 by Home Ministry resolution (not by act). Successor to Delhi Special Police Establishment (DSPE) 1941. Santhanam Committee (1962) recommended its creation. India's premier investigating agency. Controversial 'caged parrot' (SC 2013).

nodes.label: Central Vigilance Commission (CVC, 1964)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Established February 1964 on Santhanam Committee (1962) recommendation to combat corruption. Initially executive body; given statutory status by CVC Act 2003. Head: Central Vigilance Commissioner. Oversees vigilance administration in Central govt.

nodes.label: Santhanam Committee on Prevention of Corruption (1962)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: K. Santhanam chaired. Submitted report 1964. Recommended CVC (est. 1964) + CBI (est. 1963). Identified corruption in government as serious concern. Led to Prevention of Corruption Act framework.

nodes.label: Administrative Reforms Commission I (1966-70)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Set up 5 Jan 1966 under Morarji Desai (later K. Hanumanthaiah). Submitted 20 reports 1966-70 with 537 recommendations. Recommended Lokpal/Lokayukta, civil service reform, district administration overhaul, removal of delays. Most not implemented.

nodes.label: Kaka Kalelkar Commission (1953)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: First Backward Classes Commission, appointed Jan 1953 under Article 340. Chair: Kaka Kalelkar. Submitted report March 1955 identifying 2,399 backward communities. Report rejected by Central govt due to internal disagreements + no consensus on criteria. Led to Mandal Commission (1979).

nodes.label: National Development Council (NDC, 1952)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Established 6 Aug 1952 by Cabinet resolution (extra-constitutional, non-statutory). Apex body for plan approval. Members: PM (chair), all CMs, Union Cabinet ministers, Planning Commission. Reviewed plans before adoption. Effectively dormant since NITI Aayog (2015).

nodes.label: Inter-State Council (Article 263)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Constitutional body under Article 263, but first established only 28 May 1990 by Presidential order (on Sarkaria Commission 1988 recommendation). PM heads, includes CMs, Union Ministers. Meets rarely. Unlike NDC, advisory on Centre-State disputes.

nodes.label: Zonal Councils (1957)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Established by States Reorganisation Act 1956 (Part III), constituted 1957. Five councils: Northern, Southern, Eastern, Western, Central. North-Eastern Council added 1971 (separate Act). Advisory bodies for inter-state cooperation. PM suggested by Nehru.

nodes.label: Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT, 1985)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Established 1 November 1985 under Administrative Tribunals Act 1985 (basis: Article 323-A added by 42nd Amendment 1976). Adjudicates disputes of central govt employees. Initially no appeal to HC (struck down by L. Chandra Kumar 1997). Statutory body.

nodes.label: First Law Commission (1955)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Established 5 Aug 1955 under M.C. Setalvad (first Attorney General). Executive body (not statutory). Predecessor: British-era Law Commissions (4 between 1834-1879). Law Commissions from 1955 onwards advise on legal reform. Each Commission has 3-year tenure.

nodes.label: Industrial Policy 1977 (Janata)
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Janata govt's IPR (Dec 1977) under George Fernandes (Industry Minister). Emphasised small-scale, cottage, village industries. Prime sectors reserved for small units. Decentralised industrial pattern. Reversed some Indira-era heavy-industry focus. Coca-Cola + IBM exited India under FERA dilution.

nodes.label: Industrial Policy 1980 (Indira)
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Indira's IPR (July 1980) after return to power. 'Promotion of competition', economic federalism. De-licensing of certain industries, automatic expansion up to 25% capacity. First liberal nudge. Set stage for Rajiv-era technocratic liberalisation 1984-89.

nodes.label: Essential Commodities Act (1955)
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Enacted 1 April 1955. Empowers Centre to control production, supply, distribution and price of essential commodities. List amended repeatedly. Used for food grains, edible oils, petroleum, pharmaceuticals. Core of post-1947 state control over commodities. Reformed 2020 (era-11).

nodes.label: Operation Barga (1978-85, West Bengal)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Left Front's flagship land-tenancy reform in West Bengal from 1978. Registered 1.5M bargadars (sharecroppers) giving them legal security + 75% crop share. Boosted Left Front's rural base. Model referenced nationally. Credited as WB's only successful land reform.

nodes.label: ULFA (United Liberation Front of Asom, 1979)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Founded 7 April 1979 at Rang Ghar, Sibsagar during Assam Movement. Demanded 'Swadhin Asom' (sovereign Assam). Went underground 1990 after ban. Operation Bajrang 1990, Operation Rhino 1991. Paresh Baruah (military) + Arabinda Rajkhowa (political). Peace talks 2011 onwards.

nodes.label: Aryabhata (India's First Satellite, 1975)
nodes.subject: science
nodes.detail: India's first indigenous satellite, launched 19 April 1975 from Kapustin Yar, USSR on Soviet Kosmos-3M rocket (India had no launch vehicle yet). Built by ISRO at Peenya, Bangalore under U.R. Rao. 360 kg, named after 5th-century astronomer Aryabhata. Studied X-ray astronomy and aeronomy.

nodes.label: Rohini / SLV-3 (First Indigenous Launch, 1980)
nodes.subject: science
nodes.detail: India's first successful indigenous satellite launch, 18 July 1980 from Sriharikota. SLV-3 (Satellite Launch Vehicle) developed by ISRO under APJ Abdul Kalam (project director). Placed Rohini RS-1 (35 kg) into orbit. Made India sixth nation with launch capability.

nodes.label: INSAT-1A (1982)
nodes.subject: science
nodes.detail: India's first multipurpose geostationary communications satellite, launched 10 April 1982 on US Delta rocket. Started Indian National Satellite System (INSAT). Used for TV broadcasting (1982 Asian Games colour telecast), telephony, meteorology. INSAT series backbone of Indian broadcasting.

nodes.label: A.P.J. Abdul Kalam
nodes.subject: science
nodes.detail: Aerospace engineer (1931-2015). SLV-3 project director (first indigenous launch 1980). DRDO scientific advisor — Agni + Prithvi missiles (Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme 1983-2008). Pokhran-II 1998 (era 11) coordinator. 11th President of India 2002-07. 'Missile Man of India'.

nodes.label: DRDO (Defence Research and Development Organisation, 1958)
nodes.subject: science
nodes.detail: Established 1958 by merger of Defence Science Organisation + Technical Development Establishment. Under Ministry of Defence. Apex military R&D body. Key programmes: IGMDP (1983-08, Kalam), Light Combat Aircraft (Tejas), Arjun MBT, Akash, BrahMos.

nodes.label: CSIR (Council of Scientific and Industrial Research)
nodes.subject: science
nodes.detail: Established 26 Sept 1942 (pre-independence) but rapidly expanded post-1947 under S.S. Bhatnagar (first DG 1943-54). Network of 37+ national labs. CSIR Bhatnagar Award. PM is President ex-officio. Core of India's civilian scientific establishment.

nodes.label: Raja Ramanna
nodes.subject: science
nodes.detail: Nuclear physicist (1925-2004). Director BARC 1972-83. Led Pokhran-I team (18 May 1974 'Smiling Buddha'). Member Planning Commission, Rajya Sabha MP. Bharata Natyam dancer-musician as well. Padma Vibhushan 1975.

nodes.label: Rajiv-Jayewardene Accord (29 July 1987)
nodes.subject: polity
nodes.detail: Indo-Sri Lanka Peace Accord signed 29 July 1987 by Rajiv Gandhi + J.R. Jayewardene. Provisions: devolve power to Tamil provinces, IPKF deployment to disarm militants, Tamil as official language. LTTE initially surrendered arms then resumed war. IPKF 1987-90 costly failure. Led to Rajiv's LTTE assassination 1991.
